acceptance_criteria: Human management can assign, transfer and clear a single ant owner and override membership or messenger choices. The current owner can add/remove ant members and set/clear the messenger only for its own channel. Non-owners cannot manage a channel; former owners lose authority after transfer or removal. Ant ownership grants neither ownership-transfer nor channel-deletion permission and grants no direct channel KV write access. Ownership does not change mention/messenger wake rules or human thread ownership and escalation. Concurrent management requests cannot overwrite unrelated changes or use stale ownership to bypass authorization. Focused tests cover authorized management, rejected operations, transfer/revocation and existing ownerless behavior. README documents ownership, role separation, management commands and permissions.

description: Give a channel an optional single ant owner, separate from its messenger and members. Humans assign, transfer or clear ownership and retain override authority. The owner may add or remove ant members and set or clear the messenger of its own channel, but may not transfer ownership or delete the channel. Ownership alone does not wake the owner on every post. Channel ownership remains distinct from human thread ownership and escalation.
design: Keep channel KV writes restricted to human credentials under the current contract. Introduce authenticated, validated management requests with a trusted mutation path rather than granting ants unrestricted channel KV writes. Authorize against the current owner and preserve concurrent-update protections. Define the trusted request processor, permission boundaries, revocation behavior and ant-facing management interface before implementation. Update affected canonical requirements through bd spec change before changing existing human-only management behavior. Channels without an owner retain current behavior; owning, triaging and participating are independent roles.
title: Ant channel ownership with scoped management and human override

acceptance_criteria: A standby daemon starts serving an ant within about a second of the active daemon entry expiring, without polling. ants init upgrades existing buckets.
close_reason: Roster bucket leaves expiry markers (nats-server >= 2.11, added by ants init); a waiting daemon watches and takes over within ~1s, with a 60s safety poll, or every heartbeat on older hubs.
description: The roster (ROSTER_TTL 30s) and presence (PRESENCE_TTL 30s) buckets expire entries through the bucket max_age, which is silent: no watcher hears that an entry is gone. So a standby daemon in roster::wait_for_turn polls, and readers of a stale view (ants roster, notify Present) learn of a dead daemon or device only on their next read. nats-server 2.11 KV limit markers (ADR-48; async-nats kv::Config::limit_markers, which sets allow_msg_ttl and subject_delete_marker_ttl) put a delete marker with Nats-Marker-Reason: MaxAge when an entry expires, and watchers see it. Per-key TTLs (kv::Store::create_with_ttl / Nats-TTL; whole seconds only) could also give each entry its own lifetime. allow_msg_ttl can be turned on for an existing bucket (it cannot be turned off later), so hub::upgrade would add it as a Drift for the roster and presence buckets. The roster watch in roster.rs already filters on kv::Operation::Put, so check how a MaxAge marker shows up (Delete or Purge).
title: Use KV limit markers so roster and presence expiry is seen by watchers

comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-720a8b14
comments.text:
Confirmed in nats-server v2.15.3 source and by test. Hub side: canSubscribeInternal (client.go ~3470) lets a wildcard subscription cross to a LEAF only if perms.sub.allow (= the uplink user's pub allow, swapped) Match()es it or, for wildcards, ReverseMatch()es it. reverseMatchLevel on '>' calls getAllNodes(l), which adds the l.pwc/l.fwc nodes themselves and recurses only into l.nodes, never into l.pwc.next / l.fwc.next. So the allowance 'ants.inbox.*.dev-a' is never found for 'ants.inbox.>' (nor 'ants.plan.*.

' for 'ants.plan.>', so plan interest never crossed, even with the human on the uplink). Local fix (commit 59035d2 on fleet/1at): Permissions::for_leaf adds, per persona, its sendable patterns with '*' replaced by the persona id (ants.inbox.dev-a.dev-a, ants.plan.dev-a.dev-a): literal subsets of what the patterns already allow, so nothing widens. Test in leaf.rs: dev-a-only uplink; direct bus::publish -> Stored::Hub and plan::publish(Some(0)) stored; dev-b (not on the uplink) still gets "no stream" at once (the leaf filters by the uplink's perms before forwarding); ANTS holds 2. Existing uplink creds need re-issuing (ants auth leaf). Upstream bug report draft (nats-io/nats-server): Title: Leafnode: hub wildcard interest not propagated when the leaf user's publish allow has '*' before its last token (ReverseMatch/getAllNodes skips pwc/fwc subtrees) Version: v2.15.3 Repro: hub.conf: port: 4222 leafnodes { port: 7422, authorization { users = [ { user: leaf, password: leaf, permissions: { publish: { allow: ["foo.*.bar"] }, subscribe: { allow: ["_INBOX.>"] } } } ] } } leaf.conf: port: 4223 leafnodes { remotes = [ { url: "nats://leaf:leaf@127.0.0.1:7422" } ] } 1. hub: nats -s nats://127.0.0.1:4222 sub 'foo.>' 2. leaf: nats -s nats://127.0.0.1:4223 pub foo.x.bar hi Result: nothing received on the hub (no LS+ for foo.> reaches the leaf; a request gets "no responders"). Adding the literal allow "foo.x.bar" makes it work; so does a hub sub on "foo.x.*" (literal path through reverseMatchLevel). Expected: foo.> interest crosses, since its subject space overlaps an allowed subject; the hub still checks each inbound LMSG against the permissions (leafMsgAllowed). Cause: server/sublist.go getAllNodes() adds l.pwc and l.fwc but does not recurse into l.pwc.next, so allowances below a '*' token are never reported by ReverseMatch for a '>' query. Suggested fix: in getAllNodes, `if l.pwc != nil { addNodeToResults(l.pwc, results); getAllNodes(l.pwc.next, results) }`.

description: nats-server 2.15.3 propagates the hub stream's interest (ants.inbox.>, ants.plan.>) to a leaf only if the uplink's publish allowances ReverseMatch it; ReverseMatch (sublist.go getAllNodes) misses allowances with '*' before the last token such as 'ants.inbox.*.dev-a'. Without human in the uplink credentials, a persona's direct publishes from the leaf find no stream and go through the outbox even with the uplink up (and before ants-0ul, failed outright unless a hub client had a narrower live subscription). Investigate: report upstream, or a different subject layout / extra allowance that matches without widening what the leaf may publish.
title: Let the hub stream's interest cross a leaf uplink without the human's allowances

An ant-created thread uses the configured escalation chain of its creating ant without a new coordinator role; delegated work has a documented and tested origin-chain selection rule. design: Reuse existing escalation machinery, including chain lookup, leader progression, visited-target protection, max_escalation_hops, timeouts, turn budgets and persisted escalation state. Preserve established human-owned thread behavior and human-only allowance renewal rules. No change to channel mention/messenger wake rules is implied.

description:
ants-ldc3 and ants-d42q verified the Linux Secret Service store (secret-tool) with GNOME Keyring, KDE Wallet and KeePassXC in Debian containers; no WSL 2 machine was reachable. On a Windows host with WSL 2 (Ubuntu 24.04 image), build or install ants for linux and run nats-server with `ants auth init` and `ants auth user alice --human` (ANTS_AUTH_DIR set), then:
1. Without systemd (`[boot] systemd=false` in /etc/wsl.conf, `wsl --shutdown`): `ants keys store alice.creds` must fail naming a missing D-Bus session bus, leaving the file as it was; `ants doctor` likewise.
2. With systemd (`[boot] systemd=true`, the default of recent Ubuntu images): install libsecret-tools, gnome-keyring and dbus-user-session; check `echo $DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS` and that $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/bus exists; create and unlock the login keyring with `printf %s "$PW" | gnome-keyring-daemon --replace --unlock --components=secrets`.
3. Round trip: `ants keys store`, `secret-tool search service ants account KEY`, `ants doctor` (seed in the OS credential store), `ants keys unstore` (file byte-identical to the original), `ants keys store` again, `ants keys remove` (file and entry gone).
4. Locked case: store again, lock the keyring (`gdbus call --session --dest org.freedesktop.secrets --object-path /org/freedesktop/secrets --method org.freedesktop.Secret.Service.Lock "[\"/org/freedesktop/secrets/collection/login\"]"`), then `ants doctor`, `ants keys unstore` and `ants keys remove` must fail as a locked store (not available yet) and keep the file; note whether a prompt appears (WSLg) and that a run without an answer fails after 60 s.
5. A systemd user service (the daemon unit of `scripts/install-units.sh`, its config naming an ant whose credentials seed is stored) reading a stored seed after `wsl --shutdown` and a new login, waiting while the keyring is locked and connecting once it is unlocked.
6. Confirm ants in WSL cannot reach the Windows Credential Manager, and that the README WSL bullet under "Private keys in the OS credential store" holds; correct it otherwise.
title: Verify the Secret Service key store on WSL 2

description: registry.global-min-publish-age (1.100) makes the resolver ignore crate versions newer than a set age unless already in Cargo.lock, complementing deny.toml. build.warnings = "deny" (1.97) can replace the -D warnings flag in .github/workflows/ci.yml. description: The interface between ants and the system holding an ant's identity, memories and work: built-in sugar or a replacement.
title: Memory and work providers

The provider protocol is JSON-RPC 2.0 over a provider process's standard input and output, its types in ants-proto; initialize exchanges protocol versions and capabilities (tools, context, events, wake, memories, export), and ants uses only the capabilities both sides declare.
A provider never reads an ant's messages, prompts or replies: it sees only its own tool calls, the lifecycle events, and what the ant passes it.
The config's provider setting, for an ant or the whole file, is sugar (the default), a command for an external provider, an MCP server command whose tools serve as a tools-only provider, or none.

The daemon starts each external provider once per machine, restarts it with exponential backoff from 1 s to 60 s when it exits, and offers its tools only while it is up, a call failing meanwhile with an [ants] line saying why.

ants serves a provider's tools to every harness session of its ants through the ants MCP server, named with the provider's name as prefix, passing each call the ant, its identity id, the thread and the thread's origin, so no harness needs configuration of its own for them.

When a session starts, is loaded, or is rebuilt after a lost session or a context overflow, ants asks the provider for the ant's brief for the thread within a byte budget (default 8,000) and puts it after the [ants memory] instructions; no answer within 5 s leaves it out with an [ants] line saying so.

ants sends the provider lifecycle events (ant added, renamed, moved, cloned, retired, revived; thread started, done, expired; session lost or rebuilt), each with the ant, its identity id, the thread when there is one and the time, in order per ant and at least once.

A provider's wake request (ant, an existing thread or none for a new one, text, idempotency id) becomes a message to the ant from the provider on that thread, deduplicated on the id for 7 days and spending no turn budget.

`ants ant memories` shows the memories view of the ant's provider when it declares one, within the existing caps, and `ants ant export` and `ants ant import` carry the provider's export of the ant when it declares export.
Built-in sugar implements the same provider interface in process that external providers serve over the protocol, so switching an ant between providers changes nothing else in ants.

Memory and task work goes through the ant's provider: sugar, built into ants, by default; an external provider speaking the provider protocol, or an MCP server for its tools alone, when configured; or none, in which case memory and task tools are installed, configured and invoked through the harness.
ants serves the provider's tools through its MCP server beside the messaging and thread-notes tools, and configured memory and task instructions accompany every prompt, including resumed sessions.
Each ant uses sugar unless its provider setting names another provider or none, and keeps its own memory and task instructions and any tool its harness offers.

sugar, run inside the ants daemon, is ants' only built-in memory and task backend; ants initializes no other tool's workspace and passes configured per-ant environment overrides to every harness session.

description: Today the human is one identity, the persona 'human': agents escalate to it, only it holds the human rights, and the CLI always acts as it. Support several people, each with an own identity, inbox and credentials, all with the same rights. Waits for the channels epic (ants-367f), which also touches the wire contract and the human.
design:
Decisions (2026-11-14):
- Identity: a human is a persona listed in KV bucket ants_humans (key: persona id; value: HumanEntry naming that persona; a reader skips an entry whose persona disagrees with its key). Any name works, not only 'human'.
- Rights: all humans are equal; each has what 'human' has today (create/upgrade the stream and buckets, read/remove dead letters, send under any sender to replay, decide approvals, set up leaf outboxes and the intake, subscribe to ants.>). Rights come from the JWT: 'ants auth user NAME --human' issues them; without --human a persona's.
- Registry trust: only human credentials may write ants_humans; personas read it. The CLI registers its own human on connect. 'human' stays a human without an entry, so existing setups keep working.
- Escalation: an envelope carries 'owner', the human who started the thread; replies, send_message/ask_agent on the thread and threads an agent starts while handling it keep it. Turn budget spent, caps, dead-letter notices and plan rooms out of turns go to the owner; with no owner, to the daemon's configured default human (config 'human', default 'human').
- Approvals: any human decides; the first decision wins.
- Turn budget: a reply to any human spends none; a message from any human renews the thread's allowance. ants-proto stays I/O-free: the daemon tells it whether the sender is a human.

Spec changes to make with the work (bd spec change / add):
- wire ants-dnd.5, ants-dnd.6, ants-dnd.7; add: ants_humans registry; envelope owner.
- transport ants-h0k.7, ants-h0k.13, ants-h0k.14 ('the human' -> 'a human').
- daemon ants-0mi.9, ants-0mi.12; messenger ants-20j.2, ants-20j.4 ('the human' -> 'the thread's owner').
- cli ants-ved.6, ants-ved.7; add: the CLI acts as the human its credentials name.
- channels ants-2mfe.6, ants-2mfe.12, ants-2mfe.13 once channels land.
title: Several distinct humans on one team

* copilot: add arg --allow-all (= --allow-all-tools --allow-all-paths --allow-all-urls), stay in #agent mode. Not #autopilot: experimental and runs until completion without stopping.
* claude (claude-agent-acp): mode = bypassPermissions (modes: default, acceptEdits, plan, auto, bypassPermissions). Caveat: Claude Code refuses bypass as root unless IS_SANDBOX=1.
* codex (codex-acp): mode = full-access (modes: read-only, auto, full-access; source zed-industries/codex-acp src/thread.rs). Upstream README installs @zed-industries/codex-acp; docs/config.md says @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp, verify.

description: Built-in harnesses (copilot, claude, antigravity, and now codex) are just compatible ACP harnesses; no one is privileged in docs or as an implicit default. ants setup detects what is installed and has the user choose the default harness.
design:
* Add codex to harnesses.toml as a built-in: command codex-acp, mode read-only, sign_in 'codex-acp login'. Keep the name 'antigravity' for agy.
* Remove the implicit copilot fallback: an ant with no harness key and a config with no top-level harness fails to load, naming the built-ins and how to set one (spec change to ants-bce.18; existing configs without harness break, so setup/doctor must say how to fix).
* Detection: PATH lookup of each built-in's command (same resolution as launch, incl. Windows .exe/.cmd/.bat); report 'CLI found, ACP adapter missing' (claude without claude-agent-acp, codex without codex-acp). No handshake during detection; the existing harness check runs on the chosen one.
* ants setup, no --harness: TTY: numbered prompt with detected ones marked; exactly one detected: picked automatically and reported; none detected: list copilot, claude, codex, antigravity with install + sign-in commands and a pointer to docs/config.md#harnesses for custom [harnesses.NAME] / harnesses.d. Non-TTY: one detected: use it; otherwise fail with the same list. --dry-run reports the choice. Plain stdin prompt, no new dependency.
* Docs: README and docs/config.md list the four built-ins in one table with no default marked, then a custom-harness section. Spec: rewrite ants-bce.14-16 (+codex), ants-bce.18, ants-ved.65.
title: Detect installed harnesses in ants setup and treat built-ins as equals

acceptance_criteria: Either ants init sets max_consumers on ANTS, or ants doctor warns when the count approaches the limit; README notes the limit.
close_reason: ANTS sets max_consumers 10000 (init raises lower limits), ants doctor warns at 80% of the effective limit, README notes the 2.15 default; other buckets in ants-hv4c.
description: Since nats-server 2.15 every stream without max_consumers is limited to 1000 consumers by default (jetstream { limits { default_max_consumers } }; https://docs.nats.io/release-notes/upgrade-to-2.15). Each ant has 2 durable consumers on ANTS (inbox-<ant>, chan-<ant>). During reads it adds up to about 15 more short-lived ones: notes-, chan-reader, deadread- and inbox spares _1.._3. Humans add notify-<human>, and each KV watcher adds an ordered consumer on its bucket stream. Teams of a few dozen ants are far below the limit. A large team would get consumer-create errors that are hard to diagnose. Options: set an explicit max_consumers on ANTS in hub::stream_config/upgrade_stream (-1, or a computed bound), or have ants doctor report consumer count against the limit.
title: Plan for the 1000-consumer-per-stream default of nats-server 2.15

close_reason: All 18 children done: ant view, admin role, host credentials, signed orders, config edits, remote set, pause/resume, restart, memories, add/retire on named machines (leaf uplink kept in step), approvals in chat, and machine naming from the config
description:
Today an ant's harness or model cannot be changed from another machine, and nothing shows who an ant is, what it does or what it remembers. Goal: an ant view in ants chat (with ants ant CLI parity) that shows an ant and administers it on any machine, online or offline.

Decisions (discussion 2026-11-16):
- Authority: a team-wide admin role, carried as a tag in the human's user JWT signed by the account key (not ants_humans, which every human may write). ants auth revoke withdraws it.
- Scope: admins may edit every setting remotely, allow/env/workdir/[harnesses.*] commands included (an admin can therefore run code on every machine). A machine opts out with [admin] remote = false.
- Offline: changes are durable orders in stream ANTS on ants.admin.<machine>.<ant>; each machine's daemon consumes its own and acks only after writing config.toml. Outcomes (pending, applied, refused with reason) in a KV bucket for the view.
- config.toml stays each machine's only source of truth: format-preserving edit, validated by the loader, atomic write, then the existing reload applies it. An order carries the values it expects; a field changed locally since is refused, never clobbered.
- Machines get their own host credentials and a persistent ant -> machine record, as the roster forgets an ant 30 s after its daemon stops.

comments.text: ants-xyb: a daemon's dead letter kept in the outbox and the copy its redelivery stores directly share Nats-Msg-Id dead-<stream seq>; landing more than two minutes apart (source retry backoff, 60 s ack wait), ANTS keeps both. Same remedy as for other late duplicates.

comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-83337b62
comments.text:
Investigation (nats-server v2.15.3, no code changed; issue left open).

LAG. ANTS (bus.rs:184 stream_config) sets no duplicate_window, so the server default of 2 min applies. The hub's ANTS_IN pulls each outbox through a source consumer. When the uplink drops, the source goes stale after 10 s and the hub sends a consumer-create request, waiting up to 30 s for a reply (srcConsumerWaitTime). After each failure it retries after 10 s x fails, capped at 2 min (stream.go calculateRetryBackoff). On leaf reconnect the hub restarts stale sources at once (leafnode.go checkInternalSyncConsumers -> retryDisconnectedSyncConsumers), except while a create request is still in flight (si.sip). In that case the retry waits for the 30 s timeout plus the backoff. The ANTS_IN -> ANTS hop is local and takes milliseconds. Worst-case landing after the uplink returns: about 30 + 120 + 2 = 152 s. Measured by instrumenting outbox.rs the_hub_takes_what_a_leaf_kept_while_its_uplink_was_down (reload-based outages, direct path back in 0.1 s): outages of 0/15/90/150/200/300 s landed 0.1-0.3 s after reconnect; 45 s -> 13 s; 60 s -> 48 s; 120 s -> 48 s; 240 s -> 79 s.

DUPLICATES. (a) bus::store_acked (bus.rs:471) falls back to the outbox on TimedOut (async-nats default 5 s). If the hub stored the message but the ack was lost, the outbox copy lands after the outage plus up to 152 s. That gap is unbounded by any window but is rare: it needs the uplink to fail between store and ack, or a hub slower than 5 s while the uplink is up, and in the second case the source is active and dedupes within milliseconds. (b) Dead letter (ants-xyb): a redelivery after reconnect calls bury_kept -> bury_letter. If the outbox copy has not landed yet, that path stores dead-<seq> directly, and the outbox copy can follow up to about 150 s later, past 2 min. That gives 2 letters, and replaying both delivers the message twice. Readers have no dedupe by envelope id: Answered notes (attempts.rs:121) live only until the ack, and the live Seen (bus.rs:537) holds only the last 1024 messages.

CONSEQUENCES of a late duplicate. An inbox message gets a second harness turn in the same session and a second reply; reply-<ant>-<id> no longer dedupes outside the window. A reply to ask_agent arriving late becomes a 'late replies' prompt. A channel post wakes or triages every member daemon again, which is the costliest case. Plan, notes and inbox listings show the message twice, and a human message renews the escalation allowance again.

REORDERING only spans the reconnect lag (0.1 s typical, about 150 s worst). A message sent directly after reconnect can be answered before an older buffered one on the same thread: the daemon queue keeps arrival order (daemon.rs ~480-510), inbox.rs:79 sorts by stream seq, and channel 'seen' uses seq watermarks, which stay safe because a late post counts as unseen. Nothing breaks, it is only out of order.

RECOMMENDATION:
(1) Set duplicate_window on ANTS explicitly to 24h. Add it to stream_config and let init_stream upgrade existing streams; ensure_stream warns like it does for other upgrades. Update the 'two minutes' wording in bus.rs:456-460, outbox.rs:16, dead.rs:23 and the README/docs. 5 min would already cover the dead-letter case and timeouts while the uplink is up. 24h also covers ack-lost cases across overnight outages. Cost: about 150 B of dedupe map per message id in the window (ddentry + map slot + id string), around 1.5 MB at 10k messages/day, plus a rebuildDedupe scan of one day's messages when the hub restarts. The server rejects only windows above max_age (30 d) or a server limit. Msg ids reused on purpose stay correct: replay-<seq>, mention.<post>.<human> and webhook hashes are meant to dedupe, and replays use a fresh id.
(2) Do not reorder by envelope sent_at in the daemon. Clocks differ between machines, it would mean holding messages back, and the lag is short. Optionally sort human-facing listings (inbox, plan, thread) by sent_at.
(3) Optional upstream: report the skipped reconnect kick while si.sip to nats-server.

description: Messages buffered across an outage land after what reached the hub meanwhile (source retry backoff up to ~2 min), and a timed-out direct publish that landed anyway duplicates once its buffered copy arrives after the 2-minute duplicate window. Measure in practice; consider a longer duplicate window on ANTS, or ordering by envelope timestamp in readers.

description:
nats-server 2.16 turns on feature flag js_ack_fc_v2 by default. Ack and flow-control reply subjects then change from $JS.ACK.<stream>.<consumer>.... to $JS.ACK.<domain>.<account hash>.<stream>.<consumer>.... (ADR-15; https://docs.nats.io/release-notes/upgrade-to-2.14#domain-aware-acknowledgement-and-flow-control-subjects). The same goes for $JS.FC. ants-proto Permissions grant only the v1 form: $JS.ACK.ANTS.<consumer>.> and $JS.FC.<stream>.> (crates/ants-proto/src/lib.rs about lines 939-1218: inbox, chan, notify consumers, KV watchers, outbox). On such a hub every ack an ant or human sends is denied, so messages are redelivered until they become dead letters, and KV watches stall on flow control.

Reproduced on nats-server 2.15.3 by adding `feature_flags { js_ack_fc_v2: true }` to the test servers in ants-test-support: 5 tests in crates/ants fail with "double ack response timed out": credentials_confine_each_user_to_its_role, clients_on_a_leaf_node_reach_the_hub_stream_through_its_domain, ants_post_to_channels_as_themselves_and_read_but_never_write_the_channels_bucket, failed_messages_become_dead_letters_the_human_replays and the_read_state_of_the_old_inbox_consumer_moves_into_the_marker. All 5 pass without the flag.

Fix: grant both forms, e.g. $JS.ACK.*.*.ANTS.<consumer>.> beside the v1 subject. Check which domain token a hub without a domain uses. Bump PERMISSIONS_VERSION so that ants doctor and creds checks flag old credentials for renewal. Run CI with the flag on, for at least the auth tests. Document in README and docs/transport.md that credentials must be renewed before the hub upgrades to 2.16.
title: Allow v2 JetStream ack and flow-control subjects in credentials before hubs move to nats-server 2.16

close_reason: ants ant clone SRC NEW by admin order: home, history, worktrees, forked sessions, new key and identity; landed via fleet-clone
description:
Clone an ant: a copy under a new name that brings over everything the ant has, including its thread sessions and thread history. The source keeps running. The clone is a different ant on the same bus and the same machine.

Command: 'ants ant clone SRC NEW [ant-flags...]' sends an admin order (ants-5ggma.4) to the daemon serving SRC, from any machine. The admin role is required, as for adding an ant on a named machine (ants-5ggma.10). That daemon:
1. Pauses SRC (ants-5ggma.7): messages stay queued and a running prompt finishes first, so everything below is one consistent point in time.
2. Copies the home into NEW's home (~/.ants/NEW by default): core and harness memories and the task database.
3. Copies SRC's [[ant]] table as NEW's, with the flags overriding it. A templated SRC gives a plain [[ant]]. This is written to config.toml as a settings order does (ants-5ggma.5).
4. Forks every thread session SRC has in ants_sessions (SRC.THREAD) into NEW.THREAD, keeping the harness it ran in:
   - with the harness's session/fork (ACP unstable_session_fork, when the harness advertises it), so NEW resumes exactly where SRC was;
   - otherwise NEW.THREAD records only that the session was cloned, and NEW's first prompt in the thread starts a new session seeded from the history (a new Rebuild reason, Cloned).
   Spend, escalation and narrowing state start fresh for NEW.
5. Snapshots thread history: the messages SRC's history reads return for each of those threads go to NEW's home at history/THREAD.jsonl. NEW reads a thread's history as that snapshot followed by its own messages, so it outlives the ANTS stream's 30 days. SRC's later messages stay private to SRC, and NEW gets no read rights on SRC's subjects. Attachments are kept as references and expire with ants_files.
6. Copies worktrees: each of SRC's thread worktrees becomes NEW's at <NEW home>/worktrees/THREAD, on a new branch ants/NEW/THREAD from SRC's branch tip, with uncommitted changes carried over.
7. Copies the escalation chain: NEW's escalate_to is SRC's. Other ants' chains that name SRC do not change.
8. Gives NEW a key generated there and signed by ants signer, as an admin-added ant gets.
9. Creates NEW's identity record with a new id and born, so NEW looks different, and cloned_from {ant, id, at}. NEW keeps SRC's prompts, so it keeps SRC's growth stage.
10. Starts NEW and resumes SRC. If any step fails, it undoes the earlier steps and resumes SRC.

Not cloned:
- SRC's queued and unread messages, which stay addressed to SRC
- its channel memberships (each channel's owner or a human adds NEW)
- other ants' or humans' references to SRC
- spend counters

Threads: NEW takes part in SRC's threads from then on. A human messaging NEW in a thread reaches NEW with that thread's context, while SRC goes on in the same thread separately. The thread view shows the earlier messages as SRC's and the later ones as each ant's own.

Refusals: NEW already has an identity record or a [[ant]] table on that machine; SRC is not served, or is marked moved.

Docs: README command table (ants ant clone), config.md (what a clone carries), hooks.md if the roster or identity output changes.
title: Clone an ant under a new name with its sessions and thread history

close_reason: Per-human read marker in KV ants_read (CAS), replies no longer consumed; inbox -f fans out to every device; device UUIDv7 + label in JWT tag; ants auth devices/rename, revoke --device; migration from inbox-<name> (51d1629)
description:
One human can use several devices today (ants auth user NAME --human issues a new key per run; earlier creds stay valid), but all share the durable pull consumer inbox-<name>: a reply read on one device is acked and never reaches the others, two ants inbox -f sessions split replies between them, and messages peeked on one device stay hidden from the others for ACK_WAIT (60s).

Wanted: every device of a human sees every reply. Live delivery fans out to all connected devices (e.g. core subscription on the stored-inbox republish, or an ordered consumer per device); read state is per human and synced (a read marker in KV that every device honours and updates), so reading on one device marks read everywhere without consuming the message for the others. Keep ack-after-store semantics and ants ask --wait / --follow behaviour.

Device identity: each device gets a unique generated ID (not chosen by the human, never reused; e.g. UUIDv7 or derived from the device's user NKey) plus a human-readable label (e.g. 'Quang's iPhone', editable, need not be unique). The ID is carried in the device's user JWT and keys per-device state (consumer, presence, push target); the label is for display in a device listing (e.g. ants auth devices NAME) and for picking a device to rename or revoke (ants-4zlw), with the ID disambiguating duplicate labels.
title: Multi-device humans: every device receives every reply, with read state synced across devices

close_reason: Escalations, ask_human questions and tool requests go to the human's assistant first when it can act (assistant_first.rs); pass-up via escalate or escalate_after; direct to human when assistant down; away relay to assistant removed; notifiers push on pass-up.
description:
Ants escalate straight to a human that has an assistant: the daemon sends what leaves the escalate_to chain to the thread owner, else the default human (ants-daemon escalation.rs Hop::Owner); ask_human questions and tool requests also go to the human; the assistant only gets them through the notifier relay while the human is away (ants/src/notify/notices.rs relayed, ants-9ejt9.6).

Wanted: whenever the human the daemon would reach has an assistant (grant standing, assistant_of tag), stuck escalations (turn budget, caps, dead letters), ask_human questions and tool requests go to the assistant first. The assistant settles what it can and passes on to its human what it cannot.

Notes:
- Tool-request decisions by an assistant still need the human device-signed confirmation or a pre-allow rule (ants-9ejt9.3); the request lands in the human home as now, with the assistant decision pending confirmation.
- The human may still answer directly at any point; a human message still ends an escalation.
- Pass-up to the human: an explicit assistant action (escalate to its human) plus a timeout (escalate_after) so an idle/offline/paused assistant never strands it.
- Assistant down (signed out, failing, paused, retired, grant withdrawn): go to the human directly.
- Away relay: with the assistant already first, the away relay of these to the assistant is redundant; a human stand-in still applies.
- Notifier/webhook pushes: decide whether the human is notified at assistant-first time or only on pass-up.
- Docs: docs/architecture.md escalation section, docs/config.md, assistant docs.
title: Route escalations, ask_human questions and tool requests to the human's assistant first

Concurrent daemon starts cannot launch duplicate servers or share a JetStream store unsafely. Missing executables, invalid configuration, occupied ports, startup timeout and early child exit produce actionable errors without silent insecure fallback. Auth/TLS failures never cause replacement-server startup. Unexpected child exits follow the documented bounded restart policy. Graceful shutdown drains in-flight ant work before stopping NATS, reaps the child, preserves JetStream data, and leaves unmanaged servers untouched; startup failure, upgrade exit and parent termination do not leak children. Leaf reload and credential renewal keep working with managed NATS. Cover lifecycle and failure paths with focused tests, including restart persistence, duplicate ownership and shutdown ordering. Document configuration, lifecycle, logs, setup/service ownership and supported-platform behavior in README.md and docs; keep specs current and run scripts/check.sh.

description: Add an opt-in managed-NATS mode in which ants daemon starts one local nats-server subprocess before opening daemon connections, rather than requiring a separately installed NATS service. Keep external-server mode for existing services and shared hubs. Ordinary short-lived ants CLI commands must not each spawn a server.
design: Proposed configuration: a [nats_server] section naming the executable and an existing NATS configuration file; finalize field names during implementation. Integrate ownership at crates/ants/src/cmd/daemon.rs before serve::run, using tokio::process::Command without a shell. Use the existing leaf/hub configuration and persistent JetStream store, not a throwaway or unauthenticated replacement. Acquire a per-server lock and report an already running or conflicting server without taking ownership. Wait for protocol-level readiness with a deadline while observing child exit and shutdown. Supervise unexpected exits with capped backoff and a bounded retry policy. Route leaf configuration reloads and renewed uplink credentials through the managed process as well as existing service-manager paths. Update setup/service installation so NATS is supervised by exactly one owner; retain external-service support.

description: An ant a human marks as its assistant, acting with the human's privileges on its behalf.
title: Personal assistant ants

An ant acts as a human's assistant only while the human's device-signed grant naming it stands in ants_humans and its user JWT, signed by the team account, carries the matching assistant_of tag; each human has at most one assistant.

ants assistant enable creates a dedicated assistant ant for the human in one command, issuing its credentials with the assistant_of tag, adding its [[ant]] with an assistant whoami and signing the grant; any other non-templated ant may be designated instead, and a templated ant may not.

Stuck escalations, ask_human questions and tool requests that would reach a human go first to its assistant when it has one, which settles what it can and passes the rest to the human, explicitly or after escalate_after; they go to the human directly while the assistant cannot act, and while the human is away to its human stand-in when it set one.

Every act of an assistant is published under its own name with on_behalf_of naming the human, verified by readers against the grant, shown as '<human> via <assistant>', and reported to the human's inbox on one activity thread per human and UTC day, never pushed; an unverified on_behalf_of is marked forged and ignored.

ants chat lists the human's activity threads in a dedicated assistant activity list, out of home, the work lists and their counts; ants inbox leaves the reports out, marks them read unless peeking and sums them up in one line per activity thread, listing them one by one only with --activity or --thread naming the activity thread.

description:
Headless agent teams on several machines talk to each other and to the human from a terminal, without SSH or inbound public ports.

Decided:
- Backbone: NATS + JetStream (durable inboxes, acks, redelivery) and NATS KV (roster, sessions). Replaces Buzz's relay.
- Transport is pluggable: Dev Tunnels (TCP), direct ws/wss, or an HTTPS fallback bridge. Agents always talk to a local NATS leaf node; only the leaf's uplink changes.

- Memory efficiency: Rust, one 'ants' binary (CLI, daemon, MCP), tokio current-thread, harness processes capped and evicted when idle.
- Names: project ants; subjects under ants.; stream ANTS; KV ants_roster, ants_sessions.
Source: 'Headless Agent Communication Over Dev Tunnels' design discussion.

comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-d0563260
comments.text: Decided: no integrity or origin checks on a cross-bus import. Considered and dropped: signing with the ant's key and its account-signed user JWT (as AntRequest does), an out-of-band fingerprint (--expect), a trusted-accounts list, live confirmation by the source's signer, binding to a target account (--to) and encrypting to it. Only the target bus's own rule applies: an import is refused when the bus already holds the name or the identity id.

description:
Move or copy an ant from one bus to another, as an ant moving to a new job: it keeps who it is and its experience (identity, growth, memories) but not what it was doing (tasks, threads, sessions, worktrees) or the old job's role (capabilities, escalation, allow). One bus never holds two copies of an ant.

Export: 'ants ant export NAME [-o FILE] [--move]' runs as a human, on a machine that lists the ant (its [[ant]] table and home). It warns when another machine is serving the ant, because the home here may be stale (ants-v1gdm). It writes one plain JSON file, NAME.ant, versioned like the 'ants auth backup' contents ({ants_ant: 1, created_at, bus (the account public key), identity, settings, files}). The file is not encrypted; whoever holds it must protect it, as it may hold sensitive memory.
- identity: the ant's AntIdentity (id, born, avatar, color, prompts), so its avatar and growth come along.
- settings: who the ant is, from its [[ant]] table: whoami, harness, model, reasoning_effort, context and fallback. The new job's capabilities, escalate_to, allow, memory and tasks come from the import's flags.
- files: its home's core and harness memories (base64), packed between prompts so each is consistent.
- Left out: the task database, credentials, env, workdir, worktrees, thread sessions (they live in the source machine's harness), thread history and messages, and the old job's capabilities, escalate_to, allow, memory and tasks settings.
- A templated ant (request_ant) exports like any other and imports as a plain [[ant]].

Copy is the default: the source keeps running, and the two diverge on their buses.

--move seals the source after writing the file:
- Its identity record gains moved {at, by}. The daemon serving the ant drains it like 'ants retire' and drops its roster entry. Every daemon refuses to start a moved ant, and roster, doctor and the ant view show it as moved.
- Senders get the unserved-ant notice.
- 'ants ant unseal NAME' undoes the move, for when the import fails. 'ants auth revoke NAME' ends the ant on the source bus, deleting its identity record and freeing the name.

Import: 'ants ant import FILE [--as NEW] [ant-flags...] [--jwt | --enroll ...]' runs as a human on the target machine, like 'ants add'. It:
1. creates the ant's identity record by KV create;
2. appends [[ant]] from the settings and the flags (capabilities, escalate_to, allow, workdir, env and the like), the flags overriding;
3. generates and enrolls a new key;
4. restores the memories into the home, refusing a non-empty home; the ant starts with no tasks;
5. drops the harness memory, with a warning, when the harness differs.
It is refused when the target bus already has the name or the identity id (the same ant under another name). So an import back into the source bus works only after the source ant's revocation, or under --as with its revocation (a move); any other import there is a copy, which one bus never holds. --as NEW renames it, keeping its id, so its avatar and growth stay.

Identity id: AntIdentity gains id (128 random bits, hex, set at birth), and the avatar seed becomes the record's avatar, else its id, else the name. A rename then keeps the avatar, and two ants born in the same second on different buses still differ.

Docs: README command table (ants ant export, import, unseal), config.md (what an export carries), auth.md (the move then revoke).
title: Export and import an ant between buses

comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-be3b5c2d
comments.text:
Investigation (Linux arm64 container smaps, macOS bisect 27359a1..7ee2ca0, cargo-bloat):
- Cause: idle RSS is ~88% clean file-backed pages of the ants binary. Linux arm64 idle 17.5 MB = .text 11.8 MB resident (63% of it, in whole 64 KB fault-around blocks) + .rodata 1.1 + .rela.dyn 1.1 + dirtied .data.rel.ro 0.76 + heap 1.1 + libc/ld.so 1.3. Private memory only 2.2 MB; 2 threads; MALLOC_ARENA_MAX no effect; warm vs cold page cache no difference. x86_64 .text is 23.2 MB vs 18.7 arm64 (+24%), which scales to CI's 21.0 MB.
- Actually touched code is ~4.1 MB (cold cache, readahead off: RSS 9.2 MB); fault-around triples it because daemon code is interleaved with TUI/image/markdown code.
- Growth: no single culprit. __text 4.55 MB (27359a1) -> 19.16 MB (HEAD) on macOS, steady ~1.5 MB per half-day; macOS idle RSS 8.6 -> 16.7 MB. Biggest steps: MCP server 22a8938 (+1.9 MB: rmcp, hyper, schemars), images d052208 (+0.75), ratatui cc51d92 (+0.3). Own crates +6.6 MB, monomorphised serde/core/tokio for own types +3.5 MB, new third-party ~2 MB. Cargo.lock 277 -> 424 packages.
- Measured mitigations: lto=fat -0.7 MB (macOS); opt-level=z -0.6 (macOS, text halves); opt-level=s -1.3 (Linux arm64); non-PIE -0.95 (Linux, loses ASLR); EnvFilter->filter::Targets -0.4 (macOS; regex still linked via async-nats); -z pack-relative-relocs expected ~-1 MB on x86_64 (not measurable on bookworm arm64 ld). Unmeasured: skip building the full clap tree for ants daemon (Cli::command() runs twice, 382 KiB builders), linker symbol ordering of daemon code, daemon-only binary/feature without TUI/images/markdown.
- Idle is not fully idle: with missing chains/identities buckets, retry loops every 30 s re-fault NATS code.
- Options: (a) budget private memory (RssAnon / phys_footprint) and report RSS, a spec change to ants-e1b.5; (b) profile tweaks + clap/filter trims (~2-3 MB, margin erodes at current growth); (c) split daemon code from TUI/images (feature or separate binary; conflicts with ants-e1b.1 one-binary).

description: CI's footprint step (scripts/footprint.sh --max-mb 20, ubuntu-latest, run 43818215784) measured an idle daemon at 21.0 MB RSS, over requirement ants-e1b.5; README still lists 5.9 MB (Linux) and 8.5 MB (macOS). Locally on macOS: 16.7 MB RSS, but physical footprint 5 MB and heap <1 MB, so the RSS is mostly file-backed code pages: __text is 19 MB of the 21 MB release binary. opt-level=s only shrinks it to 19 MB (16.2 MB RSS). Bisect the growth, shrink or split the code the daemon pages in, then refresh the README table.
title: Idle ants daemon RSS is above the 20 MB budget on Linux (21.0 MB in CI)

comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-960d17e7
comments.text: Root cause: the failing read was dev-a's (spare reader consumers, tests.rs:243 at 6ae205e), not bob's direct gets. Reproduced under load (~1-2% of runs, 12-16 parallel copies): instrumentation showed a freshly strict-created spare (own description, new created time) reporting delivered 3/3, num_pending 0, i.e. the state of the previous read's same-named spare. nats-server 2.15.3 file-stored consumers: stopWithFlags removes the consumer from the stream before deleting its store, and the store's async flusher can write o.dat after/around the delete; a consumer recreated under the same name in that window recovers the old state (readStoredState), so read_through saw num_pending 0 and returned Ok([]). Fix (d16f1b4): reader/spare consumers (read_back, last_sequence) and the dead letter reader use memory_storage, so a new one never reads leftover disk state. Regression test reading::tests::a_read_through_a_spare_ignores_the_state_a_deleted_one_left_behind puts a deleted spare's flushed state back on disk deterministically: fails before, passes after. 1320 looped runs of the channel test under load passed after the fix. read_by_batches (direct gets) left unchanged: no fault found there.

description: channel::tests::a_human_posts_under_its_own_name_and_keeps_the_thread_it_started (crates/ants/src/channel/tests.rs:243) failed once under the full scripts/check.sh load on fleet-admin (6ae205e): one of 8 concurrent read(&b_js, bob, ops) calls returned Ok([]) instead of the 3 posts. Passes 12/12 alone. Bob reads by batched direct gets (ants_daemon::reading::read_by_batches); an empty Ok comes only from a 404 answer, a 204 with got == 0, or a first message past `last`, so one of those answers arrives under load although the posts are stored. Find which, and make the read either get the posts or fail.
title: Flaky: concurrent human channel reads by direct gets sometimes return nothing

A reader takes an attachment only under the handle the subject of the message carrying it gives, or a handle a tool or the CLI named, reading chunks 0 to ceil(size / 128 KiB) - 1 by direct gets, and accepts the bytes only when they add up to size and match sha256; an invalid reference, or bytes missing or not matching, leave the message readable with that attachment shown unavailable.

A message passing on an attachment it received (forwarding, routing, escalating) stores the bytes again under its own handle with a new id, since a reference resolves only under the subject of the message carrying it.

comments.text: Decision: the template carries the fallback list; a request (manager) cannot set or change it, like allow, env and the other fixed keys, and an added ant's [[ant]] entry setting fallback still fails the load. description: In crates/ants/src/enroll.rs `request`, the repeat-tick arm of the select! awaits `client.publish(...)` and `client.flush()`. When the enrollment JWT expires the server disconnects the client before the local `expiry` sleep fires (the sleep ends at exp plus the fraction of the current second). async-nats 0.52 then retries the reconnect forever (no max_reconnects) with the expired credentials, and a pending flush is answered only after a reconnect, so `flush()` never returns. While the arm is stuck, neither `expiry` nor `stop` (Ctrl-C) can win, so `ants` hangs instead of reporting the expiry. Seen as a hang of about 9 hours in the test `enroll::tests::a_rejection_or_the_expiry_ends_the_request` (its last `request` call has no timeout) during a full `cargo test` run with ANTS_TEST_JS_ACK_FC_V2=1. It is intermittent: 6 reruns passed. Fix: bound the flush (e.g. timeout of `repeat`) or race it against expiry/stop, and stop on an expired-authentication server error. Also give the test a timeout.
title: enroll::request can hang forever once its enrollment credentials expire

The server publishes there on behalf of any client: a direct get answers on any reply subject with the stored headers before its own (an ant may put its roster key with a forged Nats-Subject and direct-get it to _INBOX.<human>.stored.<x>), a push consumer delivers to any deliver subject, and the hub's republish appends its own Nats-Subject after one a publisher wrote (directly or through a leaf's outbox). An ant that knows a thread id can thus make ants ask --wait/--follow show a reply from another ant or human; the daemon's live inbox (ask_agent replies, chain approval decisions) takes the same path. Fix: take a message there only as the ANTS stream republished it: no reply subject, the subject _INBOX.<user>.stored.<from>, exactly one Nats-Stream (ANTS) and exactly one Nats-Subject (ants.inbox.<user>.<from>). Test against nats-server; correct the trust statement in ants-proto and the transport requirement ants-h0k.40.
title: Waiters trust a forged Nats-Subject header on _INBOX.<user>.stored.*, so any ant can spoof a reply's sender

description:
Proposal (needs the owner's decision, a behaviour change via bd spec change of the worktrees requirement ants-0mi.56): when an ant's config leaves worktrees unset, turn it on for a workdir inside a git work tree with max_harnesses above 1, keeping worktrees = false as an explicit opt-out. Today such ants only get a warning (ants-ag81).
Trade-offs:
- Disk use: one full checkout per thread under <home>/worktrees, plus build outputs (target/, node_modules) each thread builds from scratch; large repos multiply that by up to max_harnesses live threads and by every thread whose session has not expired yet.
- Branch clutter: a branch ants/<ant>/<thread> per thread in the user's repository; branches with unmerged commits are kept after their worktree is removed and need merging or deleting by hand.
- Harness behaviour: worktrees start from HEAD without uncommitted changes in the workdir, so a thread does not see work in progress there; edits land on the thread's branch, not in the workdir the user looks at, until merged; tools or harness settings keyed by the workdir path (trust prompts, per-directory config, caches) see a new directory per thread.
- Config shape: worktrees would become Option<bool> so an explicit false stays distinguishable from unset; config::to_table and the README config example change accordingly.
title: Default worktrees on for git workdirs of ants with concurrent threads

comments.text: Design. Message id: Envelope.id (UUID v7, already in every envelope; channel posts use post.id), stable across leaf and hub unlike stream sequences. Shown as 'message <id>' by ants ask/post, in MCP send_message/ask_agent/check_inbox results, and in ants inbox / thread show (text and --json). Vocabulary: a token with the user-id syntax (1-64 of a-z 0-9 '-', starting with a letter or digit), so it is a valid subject/KV token; docs suggest eyes, check, thumbsup, x, heart, rocket. Storage: KV bucket ants_reactions, key <reactor>.<message-id>.<reaction>, value JSON {message, by, reaction, at}; readers take the reactor from the key and skip a body disagreeing with it. Add = put (idempotent); remove = delete marker on one's own key, a no-op when absent. Bucket: max_age 30 days like the ANTS stream, one value per key, deny_delete/deny_purge and no rollup so no one can wipe the bucket. Authorization: reactor-first keys let credentials grant put/delete/direct-get of $KV.ants_reactions.<self>.> only, so forging or removing another's reaction is denied; a human's devices share the human key. Humans read the whole bucket (they read all threads already); ants write their own only and cannot read others'; observers, webhooks and channel managers get nothing. Gap: subjects cannot tie an opaque message id to access to that message, so an ant can react under any id; harmless since only humans read reactions. No outbox form behind a leaf: reacting needs the hub. Folded into PERMISSIONS_VERSION 4. Reactions are on $KV subjects outside the ANTS stream: they never reach inboxes, wake an ant, mark read, or end ask --wait / ask_agent. description:
Let a harness definition run its CLI's native protocol instead of ACP, chosen by a new `protocol` key (acp | claude | codex | antigravity | copilot-sdk). Built-in definitions keep protocol = acp; a [harnesses.NAME] table (or harnesses.d file) opts in.

Decisions (user, 2026-11-16):
- Selection: a `protocol` key on harness definitions; built-ins stay on ACP (no new built-ins, no default switch).
- Permissions (revised 2026-11-16): native-only. The CLI's own permission settings decide (definition args/mode: Claude --permission-mode and settings allow/deny, Codex approval policy + sandbox, agy permission mode, Copilot SDK available/excluded tools). ants sends no tool requests to ants.approvals for a native protocol and translates no allow rules or thread narrowing; anything the CLI would ask a human about is denied, never left waiting. ants' allow rules, escalate_to and narrowing do not reach these harnesses: the daemon and ants doctor warn as for bypass_permissions harnesses (spec ants-bce.46).

Architecture: each protocol is an in-process ACP agent (Rust translator) behind the existing Connector (harness.rs Launch::connect, DynConnectTo), speaking ACP to the daemon's client and the native protocol to the CLI. pool, fallback, signin, ratelimit, overflow, caps, status streaming, MCP injection and harness check keep running on ACP semantics unchanged.

Why: drop third-party adapters (claude-agent-acp, codex-acp), get structured errors and usage instead of phrase-matched reply text, and native-only controls (per-session model/effort, fork, hooks, Codex OS sandbox).
notes: No backward-compatibility layer (user, 2026-11-16): nothing is deployed. No migration of stored ants_sessions or config when a definition changes protocol (a session stored under another protocol just starts over from history, as for another harness), no automatic fallback from a native protocol to ACP or its adapter, no deprecated keys or aliases kept, no compatibility shims for older CLI versions (require the versions verified and fail clearly otherwise).
title: Native harness protocols beside ACP: Claude stream-json, Codex app-server, Antigravity headless, Copilot SDK

Native protocols count as bypassing permissions (daemon/doctor warnings name the native permission settings). Test-only stub protocol plus ants_test_support::StubCli drive resume, fork, overflow retry, cancel, sign-in, limits, status/spend, MCP and approval denial tests. description:
Foundation for the native protocols (see epic).

- Harness definition key `protocol` (default "acp"); an unknown value fails the config load naming the file; per-protocol key validation (`mode` maps to the CLI's native permission mode).
- Harness::agent() returns, for a non-ACP protocol, an in-process ACP agent (DynConnectTo) that spawns the native process (same command resolution, env layering and Windows .cmd lookup as today, no shell) and translates.
- Shared translator plumbing: JSON-lines/JSON-RPC child process I/O on current-thread tokio; mapping native session ids to ACP SessionId (stored in ants_sessions as today); session/new, session/load, session/fork (advertised only when supported), session/prompt, session/cancel (native interrupt, else kill + grace), set_mode/config options for model/effort/context; SessionUpdate emission (agent message/thought chunks, tool call + updates, plan, usage_update with cost); no RequestPermission requests: a native approval request is answered deny (or the CLI is run so it never asks) and logged.
- Error mapping so existing classifiers work: not signed in -> ACP AUTH_REQUIRED (-32000); provider limits/quota/context overflow -> ACP errors whose message carries the native error text (and status code) for ratelimit::classify and overflow detection.
- MCP: translate ACP McpServer (stdio/http) into each CLI's per-run MCP config.
- initialize: agent_info names the native CLI and version; auth methods offer the definition's sign_in.
- Test support: a stub native CLI per protocol in ants-test-support (or a generic scripted JSONL stub) driving harness/pool tests without real CLIs.
- Docs: docs/config.md documents `protocol` and per-protocol behaviour; README harness section mentions it.
- Spec: add harness requirements for the protocol key (bd spec add ants-bce --from <this>).
- Permissions are native-only: a non-ACP protocol counts as running tools without asking ants (Harness::bypasses_permissions / unenforced), so the daemon and ants doctor warn of allow rules other than '*', escalate_to and webhook/schedule narrowing on its ants, naming the definition's native permission settings as the place to restrict tools.
notes: No backward-compatibility layer (user, 2026-11-16): nothing is deployed. No migration of stored ants_sessions or config when a definition changes protocol (a session stored under another protocol just starts over from history, as for another harness), no automatic fallback from a native protocol to ACP or its adapter, no deprecated keys or aliases kept, no compatibility shims for older CLI versions (require the versions verified and fail clearly otherwise).
title: Harness protocol key and in-process ACP translator framework for native CLIs

comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-9542a305
comments.text:
Observed with claude 2.1.325 (haiku) beyond the research notes:
(1) A fork is not on disk until its first message. Sending {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[]},"shouldQuery":false} to a `--resume P --fork-session --session-id F` process writes F.jsonl with the parent's history and no new message, and answers with a result {"subtype":"success","num_turns":0,"total_cost_usd":<parent total>,"model_usage_since_last_result":{}}: the carried-over cost the translator subtracts.
(2) initialize control_response account: signed out {"tokenSource":"none","apiProvider":"firstParty"}; API key {"tokenSource":"none","apiKeySource":"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY","apiProvider":"firstParty"}; claude.ai login {"email","organization","subscriptionType","apiProvider":"firstParty"}; Bedrock {"apiProvider":"bedrock"}.
(3) control_request mcp_set_servers {"servers":{name:cfg}} answers {"added":["ants"],"removed":[],"errors":{}}; the servers are connected at the next init (stdio, and the ants streamable HTTP server, both worked).
(4) cost-state (totalCostUSD) is written to the transcript only when the process exits normally: after SIGKILL the next --resume restores less.
(5) Closing stdin needs the fd dropped: tokio ChildStdin::shutdown does not close it (JsonWriter::close fixed to drop the writer).
(6) --effort bogus only warns on stderr and is ignored. (7) CLAUDECODE=1 in the environment does not affect -p.

description:
Drive Copilot CLI through the first-party Rust SDK (crates.io github-copilot-sdk, MIT, github/copilot-sdk) over its JSON-RPC server mode instead of `copilot --acp`.

- CLI path: pass the definition's resolved command (COPILOT_CLI_PATH / client option); the SDK does not search PATH.
- Check SDK <-> CLI protocol version coupling: fail clearly (StartFailed naming both versions) on mismatch.
- Sessions: create/resume per thread; fork if the SDK offers it, else reseed.
- Settings: model, reasoning effort and context per session (no launch-time-only limitation as with --acp).
- Permissions (native-only): the definition chooses Copilot's tools (SDK available/excluded tools, mirroring --allow-tool/--deny-tool); the SDK permission handler approves every enabled tool and denies the rest, never asking ants.
- MCP: session MCP servers via the SDK's session config (consider in-process custom tools later; out of scope here).
- Events -> ACP updates (message/reasoning deltas, tool calls, usage/cost); typed errors -> auth (sign_in `copilot login`), rate limit vs quota (weekly limit, premium requests), context overflow.
- Cancel: session abort.
- current-thread tokio compatibility (crate uses tokio rt without multi-thread).

close_reason: Decided by Quang Le on 2026-11-17; memory spec changed, provider and sugar specs and phased work filed.
description: Quang Le, 2026-11-17: "let make sugar a core part of ants, but create generic interface so other system can also replace sugar if user want"; earlier: "sugar is made for ant so there should be no human involvement or approval". Choices: crate in the ants workspace, data on the bus, provider protocol over JSON-RPC.
design:
sugar gives each ant an identity, memories and work of its own for its whole life.

Research (surveys of 2026-11-17, kept with the sugar prototype repository, ~/src/sugar/docs/research):
- Memory systems converged on: identity as a record (persona, card, user model, curated core, skills: OpenClaw, Hermes, Letta);
  a small always-loaded core plus on-demand search; curated explicit writes over capture-everything; append and supersede;
  provenance the model cannot write; citations verified before use (Copilot Memory); a secret sanitizer on writes (Hindsight);
  decay and votes; background consolidation ("dreaming"); lexical search first (BM25 matches vectors on LongMemEval-S);
  skills as procedural memory. Nobody documents an agent's retirement and revival.
- Work trackers (beads, Gas Town, Claude Code teams, bd-sync) solved shared queues; none treats an agent's own promises,
  self-reminders that wake it, handoffs or resumption as first-class. That is sugar's focus.
- bd-sync is the reference for leases with fencing tokens, revision compare-and-set, the gapless event log and as-of.

Decisions:
- sugar is part of ants: a crate in this workspace compiled into the ants binary, run inside the daemon serving each ant.
- A provider interface makes it replaceable: built-in sugar implements it in process; external providers speak the same
  interface as JSON-RPC over stdio (like ACP); any MCP server can serve as a tools-only provider; or none.
- An ant's sugar data is an event log on the ants bus with a rebuildable SQLite FTS5 cache in its home, so it follows the
  ant across machines, standby takeover and buses with no replication work.
- No human involvement: no approvals, gates or notifications. The ant governs itself; persona and skill changes take effect
  only when a later dream of the ant confirms them; a hash chain over events gives tamper evidence.
- No language model inside sugar: the daemon does mechanical maintenance and wakes the ant for judgment work.
- The daemon schedules itself and wakes the ant on time and condition triggers (GitHub, bd, git, files, commands, sugar
  events).
title: Decide: sugar becomes ants' built-in identity, memory and work provider, behind a provider protocol

description:
reading::read_by_gets (crates/ants-daemon/src/reading.rs) makes one STREAM.MSG.GET round trip per message for every read a human makes: ants thread list/show (which scans every message in the --since window), ants inbox, ants channel read, ants tools list, and the ask/post --wait polls. nats-server 2.11 batch direct get (ADR-31) answers up to N messages per request: $JS.API.DIRECT.GET.ANTS with {"batch":N,"next_by_subj":filter,"seq"|"start_time","up_to_seq":last,"max_bytes"}. Messages stream back and a 204 EOB status with Nats-Num-Pending/Nats-Last-Sequence ends the batch. multi_last could also fetch the last decision of many approval requests in one request (ants tools list).

async-nats 0.52 has no batch direct get API (DirectGetRequest carries only seq/last_by_subj/next_by_subj). Either do a raw request over a subscription to an inbox, or use synadia orbit jetstream-extra, which pins async-nats 0.48 and so would pull in a second copy: avoid that. Human credentials would need $JS.API.DIRECT.GET.ANTS (no subject suffix). That grants nothing beyond today, since STREAM.MSG.GET already takes any sequence. Credentials need a PERMISSIONS_VERSION bump, and an outdated human must fall back to STREAM.MSG.GET.
title: Read the stream back with batched direct gets instead of one STREAM.MSG.GET per message

description: Each persona may name agents to escalate to. The first is the leader. The group tries to resolve the issue; when it cannot, the leader escalates up its own chain, until a persona with no chain hands it to the thread's owner (a human, ants-548b).
design:
Decisions (2026-11-14):
- Config: persona key escalate_to = [leader, member, ...], optional; the first entry leads. Published in the roster entry, so any daemon can follow a chain past an offline leader.
- Triggers: everything that goes to the human today (turn budget spent, caps reached, plan room out of turns, dead-letter notices, tool approvals) goes to the persona's chain first; plus an MCP tool escalate(issue) an agent calls when stuck.
- Group: fan-out. Every member gets the escalation; they coordinate in the thread's plan room; only the leader resolves (answers the stuck agent on its thread) or escalates further (escalate tool, or automatically when the group spends its budget or caps).
- Loops: the escalation records the personas it went through and its level; a target already visited, or more than max_escalation_hops (default 3), goes straight to the owner.
- Budget: a resolution from an agent gives the stuck thread a fresh turn budget and allowance at most once per chain level; the next spend escalates one level higher. Only a human resets the level. The level lives with the thread's spend in ants_sessions so restarts keep it.
- Offline: targets are not skipped; JetStream holds the escalation. With no resolution within escalate_after (config), the escalating daemon escalates one level higher (the leader's chain from the roster).
- Approvals: tool requests go up the chain too. An agent's decision travels as a message from a persona in the requester's escalate_to; the requesting daemon accepts decisions only from its own chain (sender pinned by subject), so persona credentials need no rights on ants.approvals.<other>.*. Humans can still decide directly; the first decision wins.
- Visibility: ants watch and the roster show escalations and chains.

Spec changes to make with the work: daemon ants-0mi.9, ants-0mi.12; wire ants-dnd.6; messenger ants-20j.2, ants-20j.4 ('to the human' -> 'up the persona's chain, ending at the thread's owner'); memory spec gains the escalate tool; transport ants-h0k approvals requirement if it names the human only.
title: Escalation chains: agents escalate to agents before a human

comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-63a6cadf
comments.text:
Hand-off from .1/.4 (branch fleet-templates, commits d5b7b92, e9b9df7).

DATA MODEL. crates/ants-daemon/src/template.rs: AntTemplate (from [[ant_template]], deny_unknown_fields): name, managers (exact ant names, empty = nobody), name (glob, '<manager>' placeholder, e.g. '<manager>-*'), harnesses, models (model ID -> highest Effort; Effort low<medium<high<xhigh<max), contexts, allow (fixed rules), allow_sets (name -> rules), ceilings max_thread_cost/tokens, max_daily_cost/tokens, max_harnesses, prompt_timeout, max_tool_calls (template value is both default and ceiling; 0 = unlimited only if the template is 0), max_ants, pool_daily_cost/tokens, plus fixed env, worktrees, idle_timeout, approval_timeout, spend_warn_percent. A templated [[ant]] carries only TEMPLATED_KEYS (name, template, added_by, creds, nats, js_domain) + template::REQUEST_KEYS; any other key -> 'ant X: KEY comes from template T'. Resolved ant: escalate_to=[manager], allow_tools=false, allow = template allow + chosen sets. Checked at load and on reload (config::check_added: max_ants, an added ant is never a manager, pool membership).

CHECK API (call from request_ant .2 and the approval signer .3):
- Loaded::check_request(&self, manager, name, template, &Request) -> Result<Ant>: template exists, manager listed in managers and not itself added, name free (no ant/schedule), name fits pattern, count < max_ants, then AntTemplate::resolve. Resolves ~/relative workdir against the config dir.
- AntTemplate::resolve(manager, name, &Request) -> Result<Ant>; errors name the violated bound.
- template::Request: serde deny_unknown_fields, so it deserializes from JSON too (prompt_timeout is a duration string like '10m').
- config::template_entry(name, template, manager, creds: Option<&Path>, &Request) -> Result<String> renders the minimal [[ant]] TOML; config::append re-parses the whole file, so the write is re-checked.

POOL (.4): caps::Pool {template, daily_cost, daily_tokens, members: Members(Arc<RwLock<Vec<UserId>>>)} on daemon::Config.pool; Ledger::with_pool. Total = sum of every member's <ant>.day.<today> in ants_sessions (own day from memory); read errors warn and fail open. Pool warning once/day via DaySpend.pool_warned. Members compares equal always; serve::reconcile replaces members in place on reload. Ant creds may direct-get $KV.ants_sessions.*.day.* (PERMISSIONS_VERSION 4).

NOTES/RISKS for .2/.3/.5/.6: approval 'always allow' (with_allow_rule) on a templated ant would add an allow key, which the load refuses — .3 must handle it. Retiring an ant (.5) drops its spend from the pool total for the rest of the day. Membership is per config file (same template name in two files = two pools). check_request's 'manager is an added ant' only sees the same file. The load check does not require added_by to still be in managers (removing a manager keeps its workers). Pre-v4 creds or leaf uplinks: pool reads denied -> warning per prompt, cap not enforced.

comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-4b4c5501
comments.text:
Hand-off after ants-o6t7.3, ants-o6t7.2 and ants-m3k0 (branch fleet-templates2: 5a16cfe, 342490c, 2c85861, e840e7c, 943aca1).

What exists:
- Wire (ants-proto): AntRequest/AntReply on core NATS ants.antreq.<manager> / .reply (subject::antreq, antreq_reply, ALL_ANT_REQUESTS, ALL_ANT_REPLIES); ants publish antreq(self), subscribe antreq_reply(self); Permissions::for_enroll_approver hears all requests, answers, files approvals and direct-gets their decisions. All in PERMISSIONS_VERSION 4.
- Signer (crates/ants/src/signer.rs): serve() judges by config::signer_templates(--config) and Loaded-free template::check/resolve_with; counts max_ants via live(dir) = issued.jsonl records neither revoked nor expired with Issued.template == T (revoke.rs Issued.template/added_by, written by auth::sign_added). Outside policy: ApprovalRequest of the manager (kind other, title 'request_ant: add ant N from template T (why)', AllowOnce/Reject), decisions via direct_get_last_for_subject. Behind a leaf: auth::extend_leaf + members::enrolled + outbox::admit_ant. Client side: signer::ask(client, jwt, key, template, request_json, reason, thread, name, user_key, leaf, repeat, until) -> Signed{jwt, leaf_jwt}.
- Daemon side (ants-daemon mcp.rs): AntAsk, AntRequester (Arc<dyn Fn(AntAsk)->BoxFuture<Result<String,String>>>), Requester (PartialEq by presence, so reconcile does not restart managers), Mcp::with_requester, daemon::Config.requester; the tool route is removed when no requester is set. main.rs sets it for serve::Listed.managers (only when the whole file is served; manager::manages(templates, ant, added) excludes added ants).
- Requester (crates/ants/src/manager.rs): Manager::add takes a process-global lock, config::load + Loaded::check_request, refuses if <keys>/<name>.creds exists, reuses/creates <name>.nk (add::seed_path), signer::ask, auth::write_creds, removes the seed, add::renew_uplink (no leaf restart: the answer names the restart), config::append(config::template_entry(...)); the reload (reload::CHECK_EVERY polling) serves the ant; Hub::request_ant waits up to 60 s for the roster entry.
- Test: manager::tests::a_manager_adds_ants_that_its_daemon_serves_after_the_reload runs signer + serve::run + Manager in-process against a real nats-server.

For ants-o6t7.5 (retire_ant): mirror request_ant with a second requester (or widen AntRequester to an enum of asks) set the same way for managers; check added_by == caller in the local file. Stopping = remove the [[ant]] entry (config edit like tools.rs --rule uses toml_edit; reload stops it as on Ctrl-C). Revocation needs the account key: add an AntRequest-like 'retire' message for ants signer (it should verify added_by == manager from its issued.jsonl, then revoke::revoke the ant's keys and push the account, as ants auth revoke does); once revoked, live() stops counting it toward max_ants and the 'name held by another live key' refusal clears, so a later request_ant of the same name works. Keep the home (~/.ants/<name>, from config) but move/delete <keys>/<name>.creds, since Manager::add refuses a name whose .creds exists. A human CLI (e.g. ants retire NAME) can run the same steps locally plus ants auth revoke.

For ants-o6t7.6 (leaf growth/restarts): the signer's signed() calls auth::extend_leaf, which already refuses past the 252 KiB uplink limit (the request is refused with that reason, nothing admitted). Manager::add writes the renewed uplink with add::renew_uplink but never restarts the leaf node (service::manual(Service::Nats, Action::Restart) is only named in the answer); batching restarts or pre-provisioning room per template's max_ants would go in signer::signed (pre-provision) and manager.rs (restart policy). The leaf's members bookkeeping is members::enrolled.

description:
A manager ant designs work with architect ants, then adds as many worker ants as the work needs instead of a human pre-creating them on a VM. Ants beat bare harness sessions here: each keeps its own memory and task tracking and can grow into a subject-matter expert across work. Parallelism alone does not need new ants (max_harnesses threads, worktrees = true); this is for distinct, lasting roles.

Safety rests on ant templates ([[ant_template]] in config) a human writes: a manager can never widen what a template allows, approval follows a policy (quota, names) or falls back to a human, total spend is bounded per template, and added ants can be retired.
title: Let a manager ant add worker ants from human-defined ant templates

close_reason: Done in d5b7b92 (fleet-templates): [[ant_template]] (crates/ants-daemon/src/template.rs) with allowlists, ceilings, allow sets, max_ants, managers and name pattern; templated [[ant]] entries checked at load and reload; Loaded::check_request / AntTemplate::resolve / config::template_entry as the reusable check. Specs ants-0mi.88, ants-0mi.89.
description:
An [[ant_template]] entry, written by a human, bounds every ant added from it:
- harnesses: allowlist.
- models: explicit allowlist mapping each model ID to its highest reasoning effort (model IDs are opaque per harness, so no 'below model X' ordering; an unlisted or new model is refused). Effort ranked low < medium < high < xhigh < max; an effort outside that list or above the model's ceiling is refused.
- contexts: allowlist (1m costs more, so opt-in).
- ceilings for max_thread_cost/tokens, max_daily_cost/tokens, max_harnesses, prompt_timeout, max_tool_calls: a request may ask for less, never more.
- allow rules fixed by the template, or chosen from named sets it defines (glob-subset checks are not attempted).
- max_ants and pool_daily_cost (see pool spend task); managers: the ants allowed to use it, by exact name, none by default (an ant not listed in any template cannot add ants); name pattern (e.g. <manager>-*).
Unknown keys fail config loading, as for [[ant]].

Added ants can never add ants themselves, whatever templates say: a manager is listed by a human, not by another ant, so no chain of ants adding ants grows past one level.
Each [[ant]] added from it records template = "<name>" and added_by = "<manager>"; its other settings come from the ant template, so a reload re-checks it against the current [[ant_template]].
title: Config [[ant_template]]: allowlists and ceilings for ants a manager adds

close_reason: Implemented in 23ff8a6 (fleet-leafgrow): uplink reconnect by reload with respelled credentials path instead of leaf restart; signer refuses past the uplink limit before asking/signing; growth measured by test; docs updated; specs ants-h0k.106/107.

comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-805df714
comments.text: Decision for leaf uplink growth with request_ant (commit 23ff8a6 on fleet-leafgrow): (1) No pre-provisioning: NATS wildcards match whole tokens and an ant name is one token, so '<manager>-*' cannot be written, '*' would let the leaf carry any ant, and hub stream interest crosses only with literal anchors; names come per request. Per-ant growth stays, measured by auth test each_ant_added_grows_the_uplink_by_the_same_measure: ~4.2 KB/ant, ~8.0 KB with a JS domain (docs now say about 30 ants per leaf with a domain, 60 without). (2) Refuse past the limit early: Signer::judge checks extend_leaf before live()/policy, so the request is refused at once with 'the uplink of the leaf node M cannot carry N: ... would take ... another leaf node', no human asked; Signer::signed renews the uplink before sign_added, so nothing is recorded for a refused ant (sign_added used to record first). Test an_ant_the_uplink_has_no_room_for_is_refused_before_a_human_is_asked. (3) No leaf restart, no batching needed: Manager::add, after renew_uplink, calls leaf::reconnect_uplink: toggles './' before the credentials file name in leaf.conf and reloads the leaf service (SIGHUP). nats-server 2.14+ identifies a remote by urls+account+credentials path, so the reload drops/re-adds that remote alone; the uplink reconnects with the renewed JWT, local connections stay up. Done before config::append so the ant's first connection finds the uplink. Real hub+leaf test renewed_uplink_credentials_reconnect_the_uplink_alone_on_reload (also shows a plain SIGHUP does not reconnect). Older leaf servers refuse the remote change on reload (logged), so the ant stays local until a restart. Specs: ants-h0k.71 -> ants-h0k.106 (signer refusal), new ants-h0k.107 (reconnect). Follow-ups: ants-vmw2 (ants add --enroll / ants renew use the reload too), ants-4sby (enroll approve records before extend_leaf), ants-rtmf (shrink uplink on retire).

description: Each ant enrolled behind a leaf node grows its uplink JWT (~7.5 KB with a JS domain, ~34 ants per leaf max) and needs a leaf node restart (SIGHUP does not reread credentials), interrupting the machine's other ants. Decide: refuse past the limit with a clear reason, batch restarts, or pre-provision uplink room for a template's max_ants.
title: Handle leaf uplink growth and restarts when managers add ants behind a leaf
