Direct to the hub: store/publish_json/notes (sequenced)/approval decisions/webhook deliveries fail with 'run `ants init` with a human's credentials'. Leaf with uplink up: the message is still kept in the outbox (the hub's ANTS takes it through its ANTS_IN sources, which bypass the stream's subjects filter) with a warning naming ants init, once per process per subject kind (ants.chan, ants.dead...); store_in_hub (kept dead letters) warns the same way and keeps waiting. comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-57e8b162
comments.text: Wire protocol (ants-yjb.5, ants-proto): a persona publishes ApprovalRequest JSON {id: uuid v7, persona, thread_id, tool: {kind (ACP tool kind, snake_case), title, locations[], input (raw JSON, truncated 2000 chars)}, options: [allow_once|allow_always|reject] (reject always present), requested_at, expires_at} to ants.approvals.<persona> (subject::approvals; captured by the ANTS stream). The human answers with ApprovalDecision JSON {request_id, persona, verdict: allow_once|allow_always|reject, decided_at} on ants.approvals.<persona>.<request id> (subject::approval_decision / ApprovalRequest::decide(verdict) builds it, demoting un-offered verdicts to reject; decision.subject()). Publish via JetStream so it is stored. Only the human's credentials may publish ants.approvals.*.* (subject::ALL_APPROVAL_DECISIONS); a persona subscribes core NATS to its own ants.approvals.<persona>.* before publishing the request. Pending = a request on ants.approvals.* (ALL_APPROVAL_REQUESTS) with no stored decision on its decision subject and expires_at > now (ApprovalRequest::is_expired); an expired request was already rejected by the daemon, which publishes nothing on timeout. 'ants approve' can read the stream with an ordered consumer filtered to ants.approvals.> (human creds may need $JS.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.ANTS... added to Permissions::for_persona for that), or look up a decision with STREAM.MSG.GET last_by_subj (human already has it). While waiting, the thread's status subject reads 'waiting-approval'. Default daemon timeout 300 s (--approval-timeout-secs / approval_timeout_secs).

Done without the tunnel (docs/transport.md): a TCP forwarder as stand-in for `devtunnel connect` to the hub leafnode port: leaf over nats-leaf://127.0.0.1:<port> works, forwarder kill/restart recovers, durable consumer resumes; hub needs leafnodes { no_advertise: true }. comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-57e8b162
comments.text:
Findings (details and configs in docs/transport.md). Verified with nats-server 2.15.3, async-nats 0.52, Caddy 2.11.9, all on loopback:
- ants ask/watch/init over wss://localhost/nats through Caddy reverse_proxy to a no_tls websocket listener: works, with and without JWT creds (operator mode). nats-server websocket accepts any path; a path ending /leafnode is a leaf. async-nats sends path+query unchanged, cannot add headers.
- Private CA: SSL_CERT_FILE=ca.pem works (rustls-native-certs); no ants flag needed. Without it: UnknownIssuer.
- Leaf remote wss:// through Caddy: works (leaf requests /nats/leafnode). Leaf through an HTTP CONNECT forward proxy (remote proxy { url }) + wss: works. async-nats has no HTTP proxy support, so ants itself cannot go through a forward proxy.
- JetStream API across a leaf without JS is denied ($JS.API.>): ants init on the leaf -> 'jetstream unavailable'. Fixes verified: hub jetstream domain + clients using with_domain ($JS.hub.API), or deprecated leaf default_js_domain {acct: ""}.
- Hub must set leafnodes { no_advertise: true }: otherwise a leaf reconnects to the hub's advertised internal address, bypassing the forwarder.
- Reconnect: proxy restart and forwarder drop recover within the 4 s back-off; durable consumer resumes. Silent link (SIGSTOP proxy) detected after 177 s with the default 60 s ping, 56 s with 20 s (now set in bus::connect). A message delivered into the dead connection's pull request redelivers only after ack_wait.
- Dev Tunnels HTTPS port as wss: only with anonymous port access (NATS JWT as real auth). Private tunnels need X-Tunnel-Authorization header or cookie; no query token (microsoft/dev-tunnels#478); neither async-nats nor leaf remotes can send headers. Not run (devtunnel login needed).
- No proxy blocked the WebSocket upgrade; TLS-inspecting proxies not reproduced.

acceptance_criteria:
* Two ants exchanging send_message stop after the reply: the original sender is prompted once and nothing goes back.
* complete() in a turn sends no message or post, spends no turn, acks the message and leaves a check reaction.
* complete() on a human's message is refused.
* ask_ant, escalation-leader answers and channel resume behave as before.
* docs/architecture.md (MCP tools, message flow) and the specs describe the new semantics.
close_reason: Another ant's reply to an ant's own message or post is prompted (with an [ants] note, even out of turns; escalate hinted then) but its answer is not sent back: no turn spent, no_reply timeline entry. New MCP tool complete(reason?) ends a turn on an ant's message with no reply. CLI/TUI render no_reply. Specs 0mi.146-148, 2mfe.60, dnd.151-153, 3b3.48, ved.236.
description: An ant's send_message to another ant starts an exchange only the turn budget ends. The message goes with in_reply_to None (crates/ants-daemon/src/mcp/messages.rs Hub::outgoing); the recipient's final answer always goes back to the sender as a reply (daemon/delivery.rs reply_for); at the sender, Hub::claim takes only replies to ask_ant calls (mcp/asks.rs), so the reply is admitted as a new message and prompted (daemon/admission.rs); that prompt's final answer, even an acknowledgement or empty text, goes back again (daemon/prompt.rs answer). Each hop costs one turn of 8 and a full prompt, then the thread escalates with reason turn_budget to the escalate_to chain or a human. The same happens in channels when ants @mention each other in replies. ask_ant is not affected: its reply is handed to the waiting call.
design:
1. A reply to an ant's own message is not answered by default: when the incoming message is from an ant and its in_reply_to names a message this ant sent (send_message, or a channel post that @mentioned the sender), the ant is prompted so it can act on it, but the turn's final text is not sent back; it is kept on the thread's timeline (ants thread show), spends no turn and wakes nobody. The prompt starts with an [ants] line saying the answer is not sent back and that send_message or post_channel continues the exchange.
2. MCP tool complete(reason?): ends the turn without a reply; spends no turn, wakes nobody; the daemon acks the message and reacts check to it (reason kept on the timeline); in a channel nothing is posted. Refused for a message from a human (always answered).
3. Unchanged: ask_ant replies (claimed by the waiting call), the escalation leader's answer and its routing (Route::Stuck, Route::Notes), resume of a channel thread after escalation, webhook replies to the owner.
4. An empty final answer is not taken as no reply: a failing harness can return empty text.
Contradicts the daemon/channels/wire behaviour that every prompted message is replied to (ants-0mi.1, ants-2mfe.56): change those requirements with bd spec change, and add one to the memory spec for the complete tool.
title: Two ants answering each other's replies loop until the turn budget is spent

acceptance_criteria: An authenticated webhook can durably enqueue an event for a configured ant and trigger normal processing. A channel webhook preserves normal mention/messenger routing; explicit broadcast wakes current members without waking unrelated ants. Invalid authentication or an unauthorized destination is rejected without enqueueing. Retrying the same event does not enqueue duplicate work, including after an ingress restart. Accepted events survive restart and transient NATS unavailability; no success response precedes durable acceptance. Webhook credentials cannot modify channel membership or impersonate a human. Focused integration tests cover routing, authorization, duplicate delivery and restart recovery. README documents configuration, request format, delivery semantics and identity/ownership rules.

description: Accept authenticated external webhook events and route each configured webhook to a fixed ant inbox or channel through existing ants delivery paths. Direct routing wakes the target ant. Channel routing supports normal mention/messenger triage and an explicit opt-in broadcast mode that wakes all current members; broadcast is never the default. Webhook callers cannot choose arbitrary destinations or change channel membership.
design: Use a dedicated least-privilege webhook/service identity rather than human credentials. Authenticate before accepting events; deduplicate retries by webhook identity and event id; acknowledge success only after durable acceptance. Reuse existing inbox/channel delivery, threads, retry and dead-letter guarantees rather than introducing a separate execution path. Preserve channel mention-only delivery by representing explicit broadcast through the existing mention mechanism where practical. Resolve service-origin channel triage, thread ownership and escalation identity before implementation; update affected requirements through bd spec change if existing human-only assumptions must change. HTTP hosting, payload mapping, authentication scheme, deduplication retention and operational limits remain design decisions.

comments.text: Implemented on fleet/caps (b63cf06), not yet merged. Design: (1) Per-prompt limits on every harness (harness.rs): wall clock (prompt_timeout_secs / --prompt-timeout-secs, default 1800) and distinct ACP ToolCall ids (max_tool_calls / --max-tool-calls, default 300); 0 = no limit. On a cut: CancelNotification, pending permission requests answered Cancelled, 30 s grace, otherwise the harness is stopped and the session resumes on the next message. (2) Spend caps (caps.rs Ledger): max_thread_tokens/max_thread_cost per thread since the human's last message, max_daily_tokens/max_daily_cost per persona per UTC day. Inputs: usage_update cost (cumulative per session; the increase is computed against the last reading of the same session) and PromptResponse.usage.total_tokens (feature unstable_end_turn_token_usage). Stored in KV ants_sessions under <persona>.<thread>.spend and <persona>.day.<YYYY-MM-DD> (30-day TTL), so spend survives restarts. All no-ops without caps, and for copilot, which reports no usage. (3) On a limit or cap: the reply carries partial text plus an '[ants] <limit>; the prompt was cancelled.' notice, and the thread escalates to the human through the turn-budget path (Inbox::escalate, '<why>; needs a decision. Last message from X'), except when the human sent the message (the notice reaches the human directly). While a cap is reached, later messages are escalated without prompting. Resets: a human message gives a fresh thread allowance; daily caps reset at 00:00 UTC or when the daemon restarts with a higher cap, and a human message does not lift them. Spec requirement: ants-0mi.12.

title: Token and cost caps per persona and thread

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Prototype: pixel-art ant heads derived from a name, drawn with half-blocks, with state-driven animation.

  avatars.py [NAMES...]           still heads
  avatars.py --blink [NAMES...]   idle heads, animated
  avatars.py --states [NAME]      one ant in each state, animated:
                                  idle, thinking, tool (call running), waiting (on a human), stuck,
                                  message (arriving), paused, offline
"""
import colorsys
import os
import random
import sys
import time

# Left halves (6 of 12 columns), mirrored. '#' antenna, 'B' head, 'M' mandible.
ANTENNAE = [
    ["#.....", ".#....", "..#...", "...#.."],  # straight
    ["#.....", "#.....", ".##...", "...#.."],  # elbowed
    ["##....", "##....", "..#...", "...#.."],  # clubbed
    [".##...", "#..#..", "...#..", "...#.."],  # curled
    ["......", "##....", "..##..", "....#."],  # swept
]
HEADS = [
    ["...BBB", "..BBBB", ".BBBBB", ".BBBBB", "..BBBB", "...BBB"],  # round
    ["..BBB.", ".BBBBB", "BBBBBB", ".BBBBB", "..BBBB", "....BB"],  # heart
    ["..BBBB", "BBBBBB", "BBBBBB", "BBBBBB", ".BBBBB", "..BBBB"],  # wide
    ["...BBB", "...BBB", "..BBBB", "..BBBB", "..BBBB", "...BBB"],  # narrow
]
# Eye pixels as (row, col) on the left half; first is the glint.
EYES = [
    [(6, 2)],
    [(6, 1), (6, 2), (7, 1), (7, 2)],
    [(5, 3), (6, 3)],
    [(6, 1), (7, 1), (8, 1)],
    [(6, 2), (6, 3)],
]
MANDIBLES = [
    ["...M..", "....M."],  # short
    ["..M...", "...MM."],  # crossing
    [".MM...", "...M.."],  # wide
    ["..MM..", "....M."],  # hooked
]
HUES = 12
STATES = ["idle", "thinking", "tool", "waiting", "stuck", "message", "paused", "offline"]
ALARM = (225, 45, 45)
ROWS = 14  # 12 pixels plus a blank row above and below, room for the head to bob


def fnv(s):
    h = 0xCBF29CE484222325
    for b in s.encode():
        h = ((h ^ b) * 0x100000001B3) & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    return h


def rgb(h, l, s):
    return tuple(round(c * 255) for c in colorsys.hls_to_rgb(h, l, s))


def shift_row(row, toward_centre):
    """Move each half's pixels one column toward (or away from) the centre, staying in its half."""
    out = ["."] * 12
    for c, px in enumerate(row):
        if px == ".":
            continue
        d = (1 if c < 6 else -1) * (1 if toward_centre else -1)
        n = c + d
        if (c < 6) != (n < 6) or not 0 <= n < 12:
            n = c
        out[n] = px
    return out


def avatar(name, closed=False, twitch=None, chew=False, grey=False, glint=None, alarm=False, bob=False):
    """twitch: 'L' or 'R' bends that antenna's tip in; chew closes the mandibles; grey drains the colour;
    glint puts the brow's shine at that column; alarm turns the antennae red; bob dips the head a pixel."""
    h = fnv(name)
    picks = []
    for n in (len(ANTENNAE), len(HEADS), len(EYES), len(MANDIBLES), HUES):
        picks.append(h % n)
        h //= n
    a, hd, e, m, hue = picks
    hue = hue / HUES
    sat = 0.0 if grey else 1.0
    pal = {
        "B": rgb(hue, 0.50 if not grey else 0.35, 0.65 * sat),
        "H": rgb(hue, 0.68 if not grey else 0.45, 0.70 * sat),
        "#": rgb(hue, 0.30 if not grey else 0.25, 0.45 * sat),
        "M": rgb(hue, 0.30 if not grey else 0.25, 0.45 * sat),
        "K": (20, 20, 24),
        "W": (240, 240, 240),
    }
    if alarm:
        pal["#"] = ALARM
    rows = ANTENNAE[a] + HEADS[hd] + MANDIBLES[m]
    grid = [list(r + r[::-1]) for r in rows]
    if twitch:
        half = range(0, 6) if twitch == "L" else range(6, 12)
        for r in (0, 1):  # the top two rows bend in together, so the antenna stays joined
            tip = shift_row(grid[r], toward_centre=True)
            for c in half:
                grid[r][c] = tip[c]
    if chew:
        grid[11] = shift_row(grid[11], toward_centre=True)
    if glint is None:
        for r, c in ((5, 4), (5, 3)):  # highlight on the brow where the head is
            if grid[r][c] == "B":
                grid[r][c] = grid[r][11 - c] = "H"
                break
    else:  # a shine sweeping across the brow, a pixel wide, slanted
        for r, c in ((4, glint + 1), (5, glint)):
            if 0 <= c < 12 and grid[r][c] == "B":
                grid[r][c] = "H"
    eye = EYES[e]
    lid = max(r for r, _ in eye)
    for i, (r, c) in enumerate(eye):
        while c < 5 and grid[r][c] not in "BH":  # keep the eye on the head
            c += 1
        if closed:
            px = "#" if r == lid else "B"
        else:
            px = "W" if i == 0 and len(eye) > 1 else "K"
        grid[r][c] = grid[r][11 - c] = px
    blank = ["."] * 12
    top = 2 if bob else 1
    grid = [blank[:] for _ in range(top)] + grid + [blank[:] for _ in range(ROWS - top - len(grid))]
    return grid, pal


def halfblocks(grid, pal, color=True):
    out = []
    for y in range(0, len(grid), 2):
        line = ""
        for x in range(len(grid[0])):
            top, bot = pal.get(grid[y][x]), pal.get(grid[y + 1][x])
            if not color:
                line += {(1, 1): "█", (1, 0): "▀", (0, 1): "▄", (0, 0): " "}[(top is not None, bot is not None)]
            elif top is None and bot is None:
                line += " "
            elif bot is None:
                line += "\x1b[38;2;%d;%d;%dm▀\x1b[0m" % top
            elif top is None:
                line += "\x1b[38;2;%d;%d;%dm▄\x1b[0m" % bot
            else:
                line += "\x1b[38;2;%d;%d;%d;48;2;%d;%d;%dm▀\x1b[0m" % (top + bot)
        out.append(line)
    return out


class Anim:
    """One ant's motion: blinks and antenna twitches on a schedule seeded by its name, the rest driven by state."""

    def __init__(self, name, state, t):
        self.name, self.state = name, state
        self.rng = random.Random(fnv(name + state))
        self.blink_at, self.blink_until = t + self.rng.uniform(0.5, 4), 0.0
        self.twitch_at, self.twitch_until, self.side = t + self.rng.uniform(2, 8), 0.0, "L"
        self.rng_offset = self.rng.uniform(0, 3)

    def frame(self, t):
        s = self.state
        if s not in ("paused", "offline"):
            if t >= self.blink_at:
                self.blink_until = t + 0.15
                self.blink_at = t + (0.35 if self.rng.random() < 0.2 else self.rng.uniform(2.5, 6.5))
            if t >= self.twitch_at:
                self.twitch_until, self.side = t + 0.25, self.rng.choice("LR")
                self.twitch_at = t + self.rng.uniform(5, 12)
        twitch = self.side if t < self.twitch_until else None
        if s == "waiting":  # antennae wave L, R, L, R for 1.2s every 3s
            phase = (t + self.rng_offset) % 3.0
            twitch = "LR"[int(phase / 0.3) % 2] if phase < 1.2 else None
        phase = (t + self.rng_offset) % 2.5
        return dict(
            closed=s in ("paused", "offline") or t < self.blink_until,
            twitch=twitch,
            chew=s == "tool" and int(t / 0.3) % 2 == 1,  # a tool call runs
            grey=s == "offline",
            # thinking: a shine crosses the brow in 0.6s, every 2.5s
            glint=int(phase / 0.6 * 13) - 1 if s == "thinking" and phase < 0.6 else None,
            # stuck: the antennae flash red twice, every 2s
            alarm=s == "stuck" and (t + self.rng_offset) % 2.0 < 0.8 and int((t + self.rng_offset) % 2.0 / 0.2) % 2 == 0,
            # a message arrives (here every 4s): two quick nods
            bob=s == "message" and (t + self.rng_offset) % 4.0 < 0.6 and int((t + self.rng_offset) % 4.0 / 0.15) % 2 == 1,
        )


def animate(ants, color):
    labels = [label for label, _ in ants]
    sys.stdout.write("\x1b[?25l")
    last = None
    try:
        print("  ".join(f"{label:<12}"[:12] for label in labels))
        print("\n" * (ROWS // 2 - 1))
        while True:
            t = time.monotonic()
            blocks = [halfblocks(*avatar(a.name, **a.frame(t)), color=color) for _, a in ants]
            rows = ["  ".join(b[i] for b in blocks) for i in range(ROWS // 2)]
            if rows != last:
                sys.stdout.write("\x1b[%dA" % (ROWS // 2) + "".join(r + "\x1b[K\n" for r in rows))
                sys.stdout.flush()
                last = rows
            time.sleep(0.05)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        sys.stdout.write("\x1b[?25h\n")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")]
    color = sys.stdout.isatty() and "NO_COLOR" not in os.environ
    now = time.monotonic()
    if "--states" in sys.argv:
        name = args[0] if args else "dev-a"
        animate([(s, Anim(name, s, now)) for s in STATES], color)
        sys.exit()
    names = args or ["messenger", "dev-a", "lead", "lead-docs", "nightly", "reviewer"]
    if "--blink" in sys.argv:
        animate([(n, Anim(n, "idle", now)) for n in names], color)
        sys.exit()
    blocks = [(n, halfblocks(*avatar(n), color=color)) for n in names]
    print("   ".join(f"{n:<12}"[:12] for n, _ in blocks))
    for i in range(ROWS // 2):
        print("   ".join(b[i] for _, b in blocks))
```

    [".MM...", "...M.."],  # wide
    ["..MM..", "....M."],  # hooked
    ["...M..", "...M.."],  # straight
    [".M....", "..MM.."],  # sweeping
]
# Markings, as 'P' pixels (a darker body shade) on the left half.
MARKINGS = [
    [],                                  # plain
    [(6, 5), (7, 5)],                    # spot
    [(5, 5), (6, 5), (7, 5), (8, 5)],    # stripe
    [(8, 2), (8, 3), (8, 4), (8, 5)],    # band
]
HUES = 12
PARTS = (len(ANTENNAE), len(HEADS), len(EYES), len(MANDIBLES), len(MARKINGS), HUES)
STATES = ["idle", "thinking", "tool", "waiting", "stuck", "message", "paused", "offline"]
# Growth by prompts completed: callow (pale, as a newly emerged ant is), worker, veteran (a scar), elder (a crown).
STAGES = [("callow", 0), ("worker", 10), ("veteran", 100), ("elder", 1000)]
ROWS = 14  # 12 pixels plus a blank row above and below, room for the head to bob

# Lightness of each pixel kind per theme: dark terminals get brighter bodies, light ones deeper bodies and outlines.
THEMES = {
    "dark": dict(B=0.50, H=0.68, P=0.38, D=0.30, sat=0.65, callow=(0.72, 0.30), grey=(0.35, 0.45, 0.28, 0.25),
                 alarm=(225, 45, 45), gold=(235, 185, 40), scar=(240, 225, 215), bg=None),
    "light": dict(B=0.42, H=0.58, P=0.30, D=0.20, sat=0.70, callow=(0.62, 0.35), grey=(0.62, 0.72, 0.52, 0.45),
                  alarm=(200, 20, 20), gold=(190, 140, 0), scar=(250, 240, 232), bg=(250, 250, 250)),
}


def fnv(s):
    h = 0xCBF29CE484222325
    for b in s.encode():
        h = ((h ^ b) * 0x100000001B3) & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    return h


def picks(name):
    h, out = fnv(name), []
    for n in PARTS:
        out.append(h % n)
        h //= n
    return out


def rgb(h, l, s):
    return tuple(round(c * 255) for c in colorsys.hls_to_rgb(h, l, s))


def stage_of(prompts):
    return max(i for i, (_, at) in enumerate(STAGES) if prompts >= at)


def shift_row(row, toward_centre):
    """Move each half's pixels one column toward (or away from) the centre, staying in its half."""
    out = ["."] * 12
    for c, px in enumerate(row):
        if px == ".":
            continue
        d = (1 if c < 6 else -1) * (1 if toward_centre else -1)
        n = c + d
        if (c < 6) != (n < 6) or not 0 <= n < 12:
            n = c
        out[n] = px
    return out


def palette(hue, theme, stage, grey, alarm):
    t = THEMES[theme]
    if grey:
        b, h, p, d = t["grey"]
        pal = {"B": rgb(0, b, 0), "H": rgb(0, h, 0), "P": rgb(0, p, 0), "#": rgb(0, d, 0), "M": rgb(0, d, 0)}
    elif stage == 0:
        l, s = t["callow"]
        pal = {"B": rgb(hue, l, s), "H": rgb(hue, min(l + 0.12, 0.9), s), "P": rgb(hue, l - 0.10, s),
               "#": rgb(hue, l - 0.2, s), "M": rgb(hue, l - 0.2, s)}
    else:
        s = t["sat"]
        pal = {"B": rgb(hue, t["B"], s), "H": rgb(hue, t["H"], s + 0.05), "P": rgb(hue, t["P"], s),
               "#": rgb(hue, t["D"], s - 0.2), "M": rgb(hue, t["D"], s - 0.2)}
    pal.update(K=(20, 20, 24), W=(240, 240, 240), G=t["gold"], S=t["scar"])
    if alarm:
        pal["#"] = t["alarm"]
    return pal


def avatar(name, closed=False, twitch=None, chew=False, grey=False, glint=None, alarm=False, bob=False,
           stage=1, theme="dark"):
    """twitch: 'L' or 'R' bends that antenna's tip in; chew closes the mandibles; grey drains the colour;
    glint puts the brow's shine at that column; alarm turns the antennae red; bob dips the head a pixel;
    stage is the growth stage (0 callow .. 3 elder)."""
    a, hd, e, m, mk, hue = picks(name)
    pal = palette(hue / HUES, theme, stage, grey, alarm)
    rows = ANTENNAE[a] + HEADS[hd] + MANDIBLES[m]
    grid = [list(r + r[::-1]) for r in rows]
    if twitch:
        half = range(0, 6) if twitch == "L" else range(6, 12)
        for r in (0, 1):  # the top two rows bend in together, so the antenna stays joined
            tip = shift_row(grid[r], toward_centre=True)
            for c in half:
                grid[r][c] = tip[c]
    if chew:
        grid[11] = shift_row(grid[11], toward_centre=True)
    for r, c in MARKINGS[mk]:
        if grid[r][c] == "B":
            grid[r][c] = grid[r][11 - c] = "P"
    if glint is None:
        for r, c in ((5, 4), (5, 3)):  # highlight on the brow where the head is
            if grid[r][c] == "B":
                grid[r][c] = grid[r][11 - c] = "H"
                break
    else:  # a shine sweeping across the brow, a pixel wide, slanted
        for r, c in ((4, glint + 1), (5, glint)):
            if 0 <= c < 12 and grid[r][c] in "BP":
                grid[r][c] = "H"
    eye = EYES[e]
    lid = max(r for r, _ in eye)
    for i, (r, c) in enumerate(eye):
        while c < 5 and grid[r][c] not in "BHP":  # keep the eye on the head
            c += 1
        if closed:
            px = "#" if r == lid else "B"
        else:
            px = "W" if i == 0 and len(eye) > 1 else "K"
        grid[r][c] = grid[r][11 - c] = px
    if stage >= 2:  # veteran: a scar slanting down across the right cheek, the one asymmetric mark
        for r, c in ((6, 9), (7, 8), (8, 7)):
            if grid[r][c] in "BHP":
                grid[r][c] = "S"
    if stage >= 3:  # elder: a crown between the antennae
        for r, c in ((2, 4), (2, 7), (3, 4), (3, 5), (3, 6), (3, 7)):
            grid[r][c] = "G"
    blank = ["."] * 12
    top = 2 if bob else 1
    grid = [blank[:] for _ in range(top)] + grid + [blank[:] for _ in range(ROWS - top - len(grid))]
    return grid, pal


def halfblocks(grid, pal, color=True, bg=None):
    """bg paints the empty pixels, to preview the light theme in a dark terminal."""
    out = []
    for y in range(0, len(grid), 2):
        line = ""
        for x in range(len(grid[0])):
            top, bot = pal.get(grid[y][x], bg), pal.get(grid[y + 1][x], bg)
            if not color:
                line += {(1, 1): "█", (1, 0): "▀", (0, 1): "▄", (0, 0): " "}[(top is not None, bot is not None)]
            elif top is None and bot is None:
                line += " "
            elif bot is None:
                line += "\x1b[38;2;%d;%d;%dm▀\x1b[0m" % top
            elif top is None:
                line += "\x1b[38;2;%d;%d;%dm▄\x1b[0m" % bot
            else:
                line += "\x1b[38;2;%d;%d;%d;48;2;%d;%d;%dm▀\x1b[0m" % (top + bot)
        out.append(line)
    return out


def detect_theme():
    """Ask the terminal for its background (OSC 11), else read COLORFGBG; dark when neither answers."""
    if sys.stdin.isatty() and sys.stdout.isatty():
        import termios
        import tty

        fd = sys.stdin.fileno()
        old = termios.tcgetattr(fd)
        try:
            tty.setraw(fd)
            sys.stdout.write("\x1b]11;?\x07")
            sys.stdout.flush()
            reply = b""
            while select.select([fd], [], [], 0.2)[0]:
                reply += os.read(fd, 64)
                if reply.endswith((b"\x07", b"\x1b\\")):
                    break
        finally:
            termios.tcsetattr(fd, termios.TCSADRAIN, old)
        if b"rgb:" in reply:
            parts = reply.split(b"rgb:")[1].rstrip(b"\x07\x1b\\").split(b"/")
            r, g, b = (int(p, 16) / (16 ** len(p) - 1) for p in parts[:3])
            return "light" if 0.2126 * r + 0.7152 * g + 0.0722 * b > 0.5 else "dark"
    fgbg = os.environ.get("COLORFGBG", "")
    if fgbg:
        return "light" if fgbg.split(";")[-1] in ("7", "15") else "dark"
    return "dark"


class Anim:
    """One ant's motion: blinks and antenna twitches on a schedule seeded by its name, the rest driven by state."""

    def __init__(self, name, state, t):
        self.name, self.state = name, state
        self.rng = random.Random(fnv(name + state))
        self.blink_at, self.blink_until = t + self.rng.uniform(0.5, 4), 0.0
        self.twitch_at, self.twitch_until, self.side = t + self.rng.uniform(2, 8), 0.0, "L"
        self.rng_offset = self.rng.uniform(0, 3)

    def frame(self, t):
        s = self.state
        if s not in ("paused", "offline"):
            if t >= self.blink_at:
                self.blink_until = t + 0.15
                self.blink_at = t + (0.35 if self.rng.random() < 0.2 else self.rng.uniform(2.5, 6.5))
            if t >= self.twitch_at:
                self.twitch_until, self.side = t + 0.25, self.rng.choice("LR")
                self.twitch_at = t + self.rng.uniform(5, 12)
        twitch = self.side if t < self.twitch_until else None
        if s == "waiting":  # antennae wave L, R, L, R for 1.2s every 3s
            phase = (t + self.rng_offset) % 3.0
            twitch = "LR"[int(phase / 0.3) % 2] if phase < 1.2 else None
        phase = (t + self.rng_offset) % 2.5
        return dict(
            closed=s in ("paused", "offline") or t < self.blink_until,
            twitch=twitch,
            chew=s == "tool" and int(t / 0.3) % 2 == 1,  # a tool call runs
            grey=s == "offline",
            # thinking: a shine crosses the brow in 0.6s, every 2.5s
            glint=int(phase / 0.6 * 13) - 1 if s == "thinking" and phase < 0.6 else None,
            # stuck: the antennae flash red twice, every 2s
            alarm=s == "stuck" and (t + self.rng_offset) % 2.0 < 0.8 and int((t + self.rng_offset) % 2.0 / 0.2) % 2 == 0,
            # a message arrives (here every 4s): two quick nods
            bob=s == "message" and (t + self.rng_offset) % 4.0 < 0.6 and int((t + self.rng_offset) % 4.0 / 0.15) % 2 == 1,
        )


def animate(ants, color, theme, bg):
    labels = [label for label, _, _ in ants]
    sys.stdout.write("\x1b[?25l")
    last = None
    try:
        print("  ".join(f"{label:<12}"[:12] for label in labels))
        print("\n" * (ROWS // 2 - 1))
        while True:
            t = time.monotonic()
            blocks = [halfblocks(*avatar(a.name, stage=st, theme=theme, **a.frame(t)), color=color, bg=bg)
                      for _, a, st in ants]
            rows = ["  ".join(b[i] for b in blocks) for i in range(ROWS // 2)]
            if rows != last:
                sys.stdout.write("\x1b[%dA" % (ROWS // 2) + "".join(r + "\x1b[K\n" for r in rows))
                sys.stdout.flush()
                last = rows
            time.sleep(0.05)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        sys.stdout.write("\x1b[?25h\n")


def still(cells, color, bg):
    """cells: (label, grid, pal)."""
    blocks = [(label, halfblocks(g, p, color=color, bg=bg)) for label, g, p in cells]
    print("  ".join(f"{label:<12}"[:12] for label, _ in blocks))
    for i in range(ROWS // 2):
        print("  ".join(b[i] for _, b in blocks))


def count():
    import itertools

    shapes = set()
    for combo in itertools.product(*(range(n) for n in PARTS[:-1])):
        global picks
        saved, picks = picks, lambda _n, c=combo: list(c) + [0]
        try:
            shapes.add(tuple(map(tuple, avatar("x")[0])))
        finally:
            picks = saved
    total = 1
    for n in PARTS[:-1]:
        total *= n
    print(f"parts {PARTS}: {total} head shapes, {len(shapes)} distinct; {len(shapes) * HUES} avatars with {HUES} hues")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")]
    color = sys.stdout.isatty() and "NO_COLOR" not in os.environ
    theme = "light" if "--light" in sys.argv else "dark" if "--dark" in sys.argv else detect_theme()
    bg = THEMES["light"]["bg"] if "--light" in sys.argv and color else None
    now = time.monotonic()
    if "--count" in sys.argv:
        count()
    elif "--states" in sys.argv:
        name = args[0] if args else "dev-a"
        animate([(s, Anim(name, s, now), 1) for s in STATES], color, theme, bg)
    elif "--growth" in sys.argv:
        for n in args or ["dev-a", "lead", "nightly"]:
            still([(f"{n}:{label}", *avatar(n, stage=i, theme=theme)) for i, (label, _) in enumerate(STAGES)],
                  color, bg)
    elif "--blink" in sys.argv:
        names = args or ["messenger", "dev-a", "lead", "lead-docs", "nightly", "reviewer"]
        animate([(n, Anim(n, "idle", now), 1) for n in names], color, theme, bg)
    else:
        names = args or ["messenger", "dev-a", "lead", "lead-docs", "nightly", "reviewer"]
        still([(n, *avatar(n, theme=theme)) for n in names], color, bg)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Prototype: pixel-art ant heads derived from a name, drawn with half-blocks, with state-driven animation,
growth stages and light/dark terminal themes.

  avatars.py [NAMES...]           still heads
  avatars.py --blink [NAMES...]   idle heads, animated
  avatars.py --states [NAME]      one ant in each state, animated:
                                  idle, thinking, tool (call running), waiting (on a human), stuck,
                                  message (arriving), paused, offline
  avatars.py --look [NAMES...]    heads looking around every few seconds (idle heads do now and then)
  avatars.py --growth [NAMES...]  each ant at each growth stage: callow, worker, veteran, elder
  avatars.py --count              count the distinct heads and avatars

  --light / --dark force the theme (default: ask the terminal for its background); --light also paints a white
  background behind the heads, to preview the light theme in a dark terminal.
"""
import colorsys
import os
import random
import select
import sys
import time

# Left halves (6 of 12 columns), mirrored. '#' antenna, 'B' head, 'M' mandible.
ANTENNAE = [
    ["#.....", ".#....", "..#...", "...#.."],  # straight
    ["#.....", "#.....", ".##...", "...#.."],  # elbowed
    ["##....", "##....", "..#...", "...#.."],  # clubbed
    [".##...", "#..#..", "...#..", "...#.."],  # curled
    ["......", "##....", "..##..", "....#."],  # swept
    ["#.#...", ".#....", "..#...", "...#.."],  # forked
    [".#....", "#.....", ".#....", "..##.."],  # wavy
    ["......", "......", "..#...", "...#.."],  # stubby
]
HEADS = [
    ["...BBB", "..BBBB", ".BBBBB", ".BBBBB", "..BBBB", "...BBB"],  # round
    ["..BBB.", ".BBBBB", "BBBBBB", ".BBBBB", "..BBBB", "....BB"],  # heart
    ["..BBBB", "BBBBBB", "BBBBBB", "BBBBBB", ".BBBBB", "..BBBB"],  # wide
    ["...BBB", "...BBB", "..BBBB", "..BBBB", "..BBBB", "...BBB"],  # narrow
    ["..BBBB", ".BBBBB", ".BBBBB", ".BBBBB", ".BBBBB", "..BBBB"],  # square
    [".BBBBB", ".BBBBB", "..BBBB", "..BBBB", "...BBB", "....BB"],  # shield
]
# Eye pixels as (row, col) on the left half; first is the glint.
EYES = [
    [(6, 2)],                            # dot
    [(6, 1), (6, 2), (7, 1), (7, 2)],    # big
    [(5, 3), (6, 3)],                    # high
    [(6, 1), (7, 1), (8, 1)],            # tall
    [(6, 2), (6, 3)],                    # wide
    [(5, 2), (5, 3), (6, 2), (6, 3)],    # big high
    [(7, 1), (7, 2), (7, 3)],            # slit
    [(8, 2)],                            # low dot
]
MANDIBLES = [
    ["...M..", "....M."],  # short
    ["..M...", "...MM."],  # crossing
    [".MM...", "...M.."],  # wide
    ["..MM..", "....M."],  # hooked
    ["...M..", "...M.."],  # straight
    [".M....", "..MM.."],  # sweeping
]
# Markings, as 'P' pixels (a darker body shade) on the left half.
MARKINGS = [
    [],                                  # plain
    [(6, 5), (7, 5)],                    # spot
    [(5, 5), (6, 5), (7, 5), (8, 5)],    # stripe
    [(8, 2), (8, 3), (8, 4), (8, 5)],    # band
]
HUES = 12
PARTS = (len(ANTENNAE), len(HEADS), len(EYES), len(MANDIBLES), len(MARKINGS), HUES)
STATES = ["idle", "thinking", "tool", "waiting", "stuck", "message", "paused", "offline"]
# Growth by prompts completed: callow (pale, as a newly emerged ant is), worker, veteran (a scar), elder (a crown).
STAGES = [("callow", 0), ("worker", 10), ("veteran", 100), ("elder", 1000)]
ROWS = 14  # 12 pixels plus a blank row above and below, room for the head to bob
WIDTH = 14  # 12 pixels plus a blank column each side, room for the head to turn

# Lightness of each pixel kind per theme: dark terminals get brighter bodies, light ones deeper bodies and outlines.
THEMES = {
    "dark": dict(B=0.50, H=0.68, P=0.38, D=0.30, sat=0.65, callow=(0.72, 0.30), grey=(0.35, 0.45, 0.28, 0.25),
                 alarm=(225, 45, 45), gold=(235, 185, 40), scar=(240, 225, 215), bg=None),
    "light": dict(B=0.42, H=0.58, P=0.30, D=0.20, sat=0.70, callow=(0.62, 0.35), grey=(0.62, 0.72, 0.52, 0.45),
                  alarm=(200, 20, 20), gold=(190, 140, 0), scar=(250, 240, 232), bg=(250, 250, 250)),
}


def fnv(s):
    h = 0xCBF29CE484222325
    for b in s.encode():
        h = ((h ^ b) * 0x100000001B3) & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF
    return h


def picks(name):
    h, out = fnv(name), []
    for n in PARTS:
        out.append(h % n)
        h //= n
    return out


def rgb(h, l, s):
    return tuple(round(c * 255) for c in colorsys.hls_to_rgb(h, l, s))


def stage_of(prompts):
    return max(i for i, (_, at) in enumerate(STAGES) if prompts >= at)


def shift_row(row, toward_centre):
    """Move each half's pixels one column toward (or away from) the centre, staying in its half."""
    out = ["."] * 12
    for c, px in enumerate(row):
        if px == ".":
            continue
        d = (1 if c < 6 else -1) * (1 if toward_centre else -1)
        n = c + d
        if (c < 6) != (n < 6) or not 0 <= n < 12:
            n = c
        out[n] = px
    return out


def palette(hue, theme, stage, grey, alarm):
    t = THEMES[theme]
    if grey:
        b, h, p, d = t["grey"]
        pal = {"B": rgb(0, b, 0), "H": rgb(0, h, 0), "P": rgb(0, p, 0), "#": rgb(0, d, 0), "M": rgb(0, d, 0)}
    elif stage == 0:
        l, s = t["callow"]
        pal = {"B": rgb(hue, l, s), "H": rgb(hue, min(l + 0.12, 0.9), s), "P": rgb(hue, l - 0.10, s),
               "#": rgb(hue, l - 0.2, s), "M": rgb(hue, l - 0.2, s)}
    else:
        s = t["sat"]
        pal = {"B": rgb(hue, t["B"], s), "H": rgb(hue, t["H"], s + 0.05), "P": rgb(hue, t["P"], s),
               "#": rgb(hue, t["D"], s - 0.2), "M": rgb(hue, t["D"], s - 0.2)}
    pal.update(K=(20, 20, 24), W=(240, 240, 240), G=t["gold"], S=t["scar"])
    if alarm:
        pal["#"] = t["alarm"]
    return pal


def avatar(name, closed=False, twitch=None, chew=False, grey=False, glint=None, alarm=False, bob=False,
           stage=1, theme="dark", turn=0):
    """twitch: 'L' or 'R' bends that antenna's tip in; chew closes the mandibles; grey drains the colour;
    glint puts the brow's shine at that column; alarm turns the antennae red; bob dips the head a pixel;
    stage is the growth stage (0 callow .. 3 elder); turn (-1 left, 1 right) turns the head to look aside."""
    a, hd, e, m, mk, hue = picks(name)
    pal = palette(hue / HUES, theme, stage, grey, alarm)
    rows = ANTENNAE[a] + HEADS[hd] + MANDIBLES[m]
    grid = [list(r + r[::-1]) for r in rows]
    if twitch:
        half = range(0, 6) if twitch == "L" else range(6, 12)
        for r in (0, 1):  # the top two rows bend in together, so the antenna stays joined
            tip = shift_row(grid[r], toward_centre=True)
            for c in half:
                grid[r][c] = tip[c]
    if chew:
        grid[11] = shift_row(grid[11], toward_centre=True)
    for r, c in MARKINGS[mk]:
        if grid[r][c] == "B":
            grid[r][c] = grid[r][11 - c] = "P"
    if glint is None:
        for r, c in ((5, 4), (5, 3)):  # highlight on the brow where the head is
            if grid[r][c] == "B":
                grid[r][c] = grid[r][11 - c] = "H"
                break
    else:  # a shine sweeping across the brow, a pixel wide, slanted
        for r, c in ((4, glint + 1), (5, glint)):
            if 0 <= c < 12 and grid[r][c] in "BP":
                grid[r][c] = "H"
    eye = EYES[e]
    lid = max(r for r, _ in eye)
    for i, (r, c) in enumerate(eye):
        while c < 5 and grid[r][c] not in "BHP":  # keep the eye on the head
            c += 1
        if closed:
            px = "#" if r == lid else "B"
        else:
            px = "W" if i == 0 and len(eye) > 1 else "K"
        grid[r][c] = grid[r][11 - c] = px
    if stage >= 2:  # veteran: a scar slanting down across the right cheek, the one asymmetric mark
        for r, c in ((6, 9), (7, 8), (8, 7)):
            if grid[r][c] in "BHP":
                grid[r][c] = "S"
    if stage >= 3:  # elder: a crown between the antennae
        for r, c in ((2, 4), (2, 7), (3, 4), (3, 5), (3, 6), (3, 7)):
            grid[r][c] = "G"
    grid = [["."] + row + ["."] for row in grid]  # a blank column each side, room to turn
    if turn:
        grid = turned(grid, turn)
    blank = ["."] * WIDTH
    top = 2 if bob else 1
    grid = [blank[:] for _ in range(top)] + grid + [blank[:] for _ in range(ROWS - top - len(grid))]
    return grid, pal


def turned(grid, d):
    """Look aside: the face's features (eyes, markings, shine, scar) and the jaw slide a column toward d while the
    head's outline stays, so the near eye reaches the edge and the far one comes in, as a three-quarter view; the
    antennae lean the same way. A crown sits on the head, so it stays."""
    head = [(r, c) for r in range(4, 10) for c in range(WIDTH) if grid[r][c] != "."]
    on_head = set(head)
    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    for r, c in head:
        out[r][c] = "B"
    rank = {"H": 0, "P": 1, "S": 2, "#": 3, "K": 4, "W": 5}  # where features pile up at the edge, eyes win
    for r, c in sorted(head, key=lambda rc: rank.get(grid[rc[0]][rc[1]], -1)):
        px = grid[r][c]
        if px == "B":
            continue
        n = c + d
        while (r, n) not in on_head and n != c:
            n -= d
        out[r][n] = px
    for r in range(0, 4):
        row = grid[r]
        moved = [px if px == "G" else "." for px in row]
        for c, px in enumerate(row):
            if px == "#":
                n = c + d if r < 3 and 0 <= c + d < WIDTH and row[c + d] != "G" else c
                moved[n] = px
        out[r] = moved
    for r in (10, 11):
        out[r] = (["."] + grid[r][:-1]) if d > 0 else (grid[r][1:] + ["."])
    return out


def halfblocks(grid, pal, color=True, bg=None):
    """bg paints the empty pixels, to preview the light theme in a dark terminal."""
    out = []
    for y in range(0, len(grid), 2):
        line = ""
        for x in range(len(grid[0])):
            top, bot = pal.get(grid[y][x], bg), pal.get(grid[y + 1][x], bg)
            if not color:
                line += {(1, 1): "█", (1, 0): "▀", (0, 1): "▄", (0, 0): " "}[(top is not None, bot is not None)]
            elif top is None and bot is None:
                line += " "
            elif bot is None:
                line += "\x1b[38;2;%d;%d;%dm▀\x1b[0m" % top
            elif top is None:
                line += "\x1b[38;2;%d;%d;%dm▄\x1b[0m" % bot
            else:
                line += "\x1b[38;2;%d;%d;%d;48;2;%d;%d;%dm▀\x1b[0m" % (top + bot)
        out.append(line)
    return out


def detect_theme():
    """Ask the terminal for its background (OSC 11), else read COLORFGBG; dark when neither answers."""
    if sys.stdin.isatty() and sys.stdout.isatty():
        import termios
        import tty

        fd = sys.stdin.fileno()
        old = termios.tcgetattr(fd)
        try:
            tty.setraw(fd)
            sys.stdout.write("\x1b]11;?\x07")
            sys.stdout.flush()
            reply = b""
            while select.select([fd], [], [], 0.2)[0]:
                reply += os.read(fd, 64)
                if reply.endswith((b"\x07", b"\x1b\\")):
                    break
        finally:
            termios.tcsetattr(fd, termios.TCSADRAIN, old)
        if b"rgb:" in reply:
            parts = reply.split(b"rgb:")[1].rstrip(b"\x07\x1b\\").split(b"/")
            r, g, b = (int(p, 16) / (16 ** len(p) - 1) for p in parts[:3])
            return "light" if 0.2126 * r + 0.7152 * g + 0.0722 * b > 0.5 else "dark"
    fgbg = os.environ.get("COLORFGBG", "")
    if fgbg:
        return "light" if fgbg.split(";")[-1] in ("7", "15") else "dark"
    return "dark"


class Anim:
    """One ant's motion: blinks and antenna twitches on a schedule seeded by its name, the rest driven by state."""

    def __init__(self, name, state, t):
        self.name, self.state = name, state
        self.rng = random.Random(fnv(name + state))
        self.blink_at, self.blink_until = t + self.rng.uniform(0.5, 4), 0.0
        self.twitch_at, self.twitch_until, self.side = t + self.rng.uniform(2, 8), 0.0, "L"
        self.rng_offset = self.rng.uniform(0, 3)
        self.look_at, self.look_from, self.look_dir = t + self.rng.uniform(2, 6), -9.0, 1
        self.look_every = (2.5, 3.5) if state == "looking" else (6, 14)

    def frame(self, t):
        s = self.state
        if s not in ("paused", "offline"):
            if t >= self.blink_at:
                self.blink_until = t + 0.15
                self.blink_at = t + (0.35 if self.rng.random() < 0.2 else self.rng.uniform(2.5, 6.5))
            if t >= self.twitch_at:
                self.twitch_until, self.side = t + 0.25, self.rng.choice("LR")
                self.twitch_at = t + self.rng.uniform(5, 12)
            if t >= self.look_at and s in ("idle", "looking"):
                self.look_from, self.look_dir = t, self.rng.choice((-1, 1))
                self.look_at = t + self.rng.uniform(*self.look_every)
        # looking around: one side for 0.7s, back to the front for 0.3s, the other side for 0.7s
        since = t - self.look_from
        turn = self.look_dir if since < 0.7 else -self.look_dir if 1.0 <= since < 1.7 else 0
        twitch = self.side if t < self.twitch_until else None
        if s == "waiting":  # antennae wave L, R, L, R for 1.2s every 3s
            phase = (t + self.rng_offset) % 3.0
            twitch = "LR"[int(phase / 0.3) % 2] if phase < 1.2 else None
        phase = (t + self.rng_offset) % 2.5
        return dict(
            closed=s in ("paused", "offline") or t < self.blink_until,
            turn=turn,
            twitch=twitch,
            chew=s == "tool" and int(t / 0.3) % 2 == 1,  # a tool call runs
            grey=s == "offline",
            # thinking: a shine crosses the brow in 0.6s, every 2.5s
            glint=int(phase / 0.6 * 13) - 1 if s == "thinking" and phase < 0.6 else None,
            # stuck: the antennae flash red twice, every 2s
            alarm=s == "stuck" and (t + self.rng_offset) % 2.0 < 0.8 and int((t + self.rng_offset) % 2.0 / 0.2) % 2 == 0,
            # a message arrives (here every 4s): two quick nods
            bob=s == "message" and (t + self.rng_offset) % 4.0 < 0.6 and int((t + self.rng_offset) % 4.0 / 0.15) % 2 == 1,
        )


def animate(ants, color, theme, bg):
    labels = [label for label, _, _ in ants]
    sys.stdout.write("\x1b[?25l")
    last = None
    try:
        print("  ".join(f"{label:<14}"[:14] for label in labels))
        print("\n" * (ROWS // 2 - 1))
        while True:
            t = time.monotonic()
            blocks = [halfblocks(*avatar(a.name, stage=st, theme=theme, **a.frame(t)), color=color, bg=bg)
                      for _, a, st in ants]
            rows = ["  ".join(b[i] for b in blocks) for i in range(ROWS // 2)]
            if rows != last:
                sys.stdout.write("\x1b[%dA" % (ROWS // 2) + "".join(r + "\x1b[K\n" for r in rows))
                sys.stdout.flush()
                last = rows
            time.sleep(0.05)
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        sys.stdout.write("\x1b[?25h\n")


def still(cells, color, bg):
    """cells: (label, grid, pal)."""
    blocks = [(label, halfblocks(g, p, color=color, bg=bg)) for label, g, p in cells]
    print("  ".join(f"{label:<14}"[:14] for label, _ in blocks))
    for i in range(ROWS // 2):
        print("  ".join(b[i] for _, b in blocks))


def count():
    import itertools

    shapes = set()
    for combo in itertools.product(*(range(n) for n in PARTS[:-1])):
        global picks
        saved, picks = picks, lambda _n, c=combo: list(c) + [0]
        try:
            shapes.add(tuple(map(tuple, avatar("x")[0])))
        finally:
            picks = saved
    total = 1
    for n in PARTS[:-1]:
        total *= n
    print(f"parts {PARTS}: {total} head shapes, {len(shapes)} distinct; {len(shapes) * HUES} avatars with {HUES} hues")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    args = [a for a in sys.argv[1:] if not a.startswith("--")]
    color = sys.stdout.isatty() and "NO_COLOR" not in os.environ
    theme = "light" if "--light" in sys.argv else "dark" if "--dark" in sys.argv else detect_theme()
    bg = THEMES["light"]["bg"] if "--light" in sys.argv and color else None
    now = time.monotonic()
    if "--count" in sys.argv:
        count()
    elif "--states" in sys.argv:
        name = args[0] if args else "dev-a"
        animate([(s, Anim(name, s, now), 1) for s in STATES], color, theme, bg)
    elif "--growth" in sys.argv:
        for n in args or ["dev-a", "lead", "nightly"]:
            still([(f"{n}:{label}", *avatar(n, stage=i, theme=theme)) for i, (label, _) in enumerate(STAGES)],
                  color, bg)
    elif "--look" in sys.argv:
        names = args or ["messenger", "dev-a", "lead", "lead-docs", "nightly", "reviewer"]
        animate([(n, Anim(n, "looking", now), 1) for n in names], color, theme, bg)
    elif "--blink" in sys.argv:
        names = args or ["messenger", "dev-a", "lead", "lead-docs", "nightly", "reviewer"]
        animate([(n, Anim(n, "idle", now), 1) for n in names], color, theme, bg)
    else:
        names = args or ["messenger", "dev-a", "lead", "lead-docs", "nightly", "reviewer"]
        still([(n, *avatar(n, theme=theme)) for n in names], color, bg)

description:
Each ant gets a recognisable avatar, the same on every machine: derived from its shared identity record, a pixel-art ant head in its colour, animated by its state and grown by its experience in ants chat, in a palette for the terminal's background, and a one-line ASCII face in lists and CLI output.

Derivation (ants-proto, so every client draws the same): seed = the identity record's avatar seed, else NAME@BORN from its birth (BORN in RFC 3339 UTC seconds), else the ant name while no identity record is readable; FNV-1a 64 (not std's DefaultHasher, which is not stable) picks antennae (8: straight, elbowed, clubbed, curled, swept, forked, wavy, stubby), head shape (6: round, heart, wide, narrow, square, shield), eyes (8: dot, big, high, tall, wide, big high, slit, low dot), mandibles (6: short, crossing, wide, hooked, straight, sweeping), markings (4: plain, spot, stripe, band) and a hue of 12; The identity record's color overrides the hue. 9216 head shapes, all distinct (checked), 110592 avatars. Further hash bits pick the ASCII face: outline (4: () [] {} <>), eyes (8: o O ^ - * @ . 0), mouth (6: v w = x u ~), 2304 face+colour pairs. The part tables are a contract: changing one re-draws every ant, so they only grow, behind a version.

Head: 12x12 pixels, left half mirrored, in 14 columns by 7 rows of half-blocks (a blank pixel row above and below for the bob, a blank column each side for the turn); body, lighter brow highlight, darker markings, darker antennae and mandibles, black eyes with a white glint. 24-bit colour, else the nearest 256-colour; without colour (NO_COLOR, not a terminal) the ASCII face stands in.

Themes: [cli] theme = auto (default), dark or light. auto asks the terminal for its background (OSC 11, 200ms timeout; luminance above 0.5 is light), then reads COLORFGBG (background 7 or 15 is light), else dark. Dark: body lightness 0.50, highlight 0.68, outline 0.30. Light: deeper body 0.42, highlight 0.58, outline 0.20, darker alarm red and gold, lighter offline grey.

Growth, by prompts the ant has completed: callow below 10 (pale, as a newly emerged ant is), worker from 10 (full colour), veteran from 100 (a pale scar slanting across the right cheek, the one asymmetric mark), elder from 1000 (a gold crown between the antennae). Only one daemon serves an ant at a time (the roster claim; others on other machines stand by and take over), so the count cannot live in a home: the serving daemon counts completed prompts in the ant's identity record (a compare-and-set on the record's revision after each prompt), a new birth starting from 0. Open: whether prompts is the right measure (schedules inflate it) against threads humans marked done or age since birth.

Identity: an ant's identity is the same everywhere, so nothing about its avatar comes from a machine's config file. A new KV bucket ants_identities holds one AntIdentity {ant, born, avatar?, color?, prompts} per ant, keyed by its id, never expiring. A daemon creates its ant's record on start when absent, with a KV create, so across machines the first creator wins and later ones keep it; the serving daemon updates only prompts, by compare-and-set keeping the other fields. A human sets or clears avatar and color with 'ants ant avatar NAME [--seed S | --reset] [--color C | --auto-color]', by compare-and-set too, on any machine; each daemon and viewer reads the one record (a watch in ants chat). A separate bucket, not a ChainEntry field, so an older daemon re-putting its chain cannot drop it. Each ant writes only its own key; humans read all and write avatar and color. 'ants auth revoke NAME' of an ant (every key issued to it) deletes the record with the short-lived account-key credentials it already uses, ending the ant, so a later ant of that name is born anew with a new avatar; 'ants retire' (whose ant may come back with its home) and a --key revocation (one machine of the ant) keep it. An ant served before this ships is born on its daemon's first start with it.

Wire: AntIdentity in ants-proto; RosterEntry is unchanged. ants roster --json carries each ant's born, avatar, color and prompts from its identity record.

Display: the head in the ant view (ants-5ggma.1); the face before the name, both in the ant's colour, in nav, home, thread and channel views, ants roster, ants watch and ants inbox.

Animation (ants chat only, heads on screen only; redraw only when a frame changes, sleeping until the next change, no fixed frame rate):
- idle (roster): blinks 150ms every 2.5-6.5s, one in five a double blink; an antenna tip twitches 250ms every 5-12s; schedules seeded by the name so ants are out of step.
- thinking (status Thought streaming): a slanted shine crosses the brow in 0.6s every 2.5s.
- tool call running (status Tool in_progress): mandibles chew, closing every other 0.3s.
- waiting on a human (waiting_approval, or a question): antennae wave left-right for 1.2s every 3s.
- stuck (failed, or the home view's stuck): antennae flash red twice every 2s.
- message arriving (a new inbox item from the ant): two quick nods, the head dipping a pixel.
- paused: eyes shut, still. Offline (stale roster entry) or signed out: greyed, eyes shut, still.
- looking around (idle): every 6-14s the head turns to one side for 0.7s, faces front for 0.3s and turns to the other side for 0.7s; a turn slides the face's features (eyes, markings, shine, scar) and the jaw a column sideways while the outline and any crown stay, the near eye squeezing against the edge (its glint kept) and the far one coming in, and leans the antennae, a three-quarter view.
Blink and twitch continue under every live state. [cli] animate = false keeps every head still.

Collisions: best effort. ants roster and ants doctor warn when two listed ants share face and colour, suggesting 'ants ant avatar' for one. Templated ants derive from their own names.

Docs: README (KV ants_identities in the bucket table; ants ant avatar), auth.md (revoke ends the identity), config.md ([cli] animate, theme).
design: Prototype (Python: every part, motion, growth stage and theme) is in this issue's latest prototype comment. Run: python3 avatars.py [NAMES] | --blink [NAMES] | --look [NAMES] | --states [NAME] | --growth [NAMES] | --count, with --light or --dark to force a theme.

acceptance_criteria:
- A host serving an ant without a shared record creates <ant>.settings in ants_identities from its config's role settings; a second machine does not overwrite it.
- A standby taking over an ant runs it with the shared record's role settings and core memories (whoami, memory), not its own config's.
- ants ant set of a role setting lands in the shared record (expected values checked against it) and the serving daemon restarts the ant with it; machine settings still go to config.toml.
- ants ant memories shows the shared core memories.
- A config role setting differing from the record shows as drift in the roster entry and machine record, ants roster marks the ant and ants doctor lists the field by machine.

description:
An ant should be the same ant everywhere. Today an ant may be listed on several machines, one serving at a time and the others standing by to take over (the roster claim, crates/ants-daemon/src/roster.rs may_start and wait_for_turn; documented in README only for the built-in messenger). What makes the ant is not shared:

- Config: each machine's [[ant]] table sets whoami, capabilities, harness, model, reasoning_effort, context, fallback, allow, memory, tasks, env, workdir and escalate_to on its own, so the ant's role, routing and rights change with whichever daemon serves it; nothing notices two disagreeing.
- Home (~/.ants/<name>): core and harness memories, the task database and worktrees stay on the machine, so a takeover continues from the standby's copies.
- Credentials: each machine has its own key for the ant (several keys may ask for one ant in enrollment), which is fine as long as all are the one ant's.

Avatars already moved to a shared identity record (ants_identities, ants-tw2yh); this extends the principle. To decide: which settings are the ant's (shared on the bus, e.g. in its identity record, edited by admin orders as ants-5ggma.6 plans) and which are the machine's (workdir, env, harness binary); how memory and tasks follow the ant (on the bus, or synced on takeover); and what doctor and roster report while machines disagree.
design:
Decided (user, 2026-11-15):
- Settings: the ant's role settings (whoami, capabilities, model, reasoning_effort, context, fallback, allow, escalate_to) live in a shared record on the bus, edited by admin orders; workdir, env, harness binary and the task database stay per machine.
- Memory: core memories (whoami, memory) live on the bus (KV or object store); harness memories and the task database stay local.
- Disagreement: the serving daemon applies the shared record; roster marks the ant as drifted and ants doctor lists each differing field by machine.
title: Keep an ant's identity the same on every machine

comments.text: Design: readers enforce. A host JWT cannot be narrowed per ant (a machine's ants change), so each <ant>.settings record now carries the ant's user JWT (credentials) and an nkey signature over context/ant/canonical fields/machine/by/updated_at. Daemons verify against the team account(s) at the stream's stored time and ignore unverified records; a machine holding the ant's creds writes its config's settings over an unverified record by CAS at its next read (<=10s). Revoker deletes still work (record re-seeded later). Without auth (no accounts) records stay unsigned and any holds. Known limits (documented in auth.md): replay of an older validly signed record by another host, no revocation check of the ant key by readers, CLI show/export display without verifying; mixed-version fleets: older daemons write unsigned records, so upgrade every machine. description: One subject per sugar identity (ULID), written only by the daemon serving the ant. Options: subjects keyed by sugar id with permissions granted per ant at credential issue, or written with host credentials and signed with the ant's key as shared settings are.
design: Decided by Quang Le on 2026-11-17 (option B). Stream ANTS_SUGAR captures ants.sugar.<sugar id> (ULID), one subject per sugar identity. Only machine host credentials publish to it and read it (stream info/create, direct gets, an ordered consumer filtered on one subject); no ant, human, webhook, observer or service credentials get any right on it, so a harness holding the ant's credentials cannot write raw events. Each event is appended with Nats-Expected-Last-Subject-Sequence, carries the SHA-256 of the previous event, and is signed with the ant's own NKey (as shared settings are); readers verify the signature and the chain. The sugar id is minted lazily by the daemon serving the ant and survives renames and moves. Humans read sugar data only through daemon-answered admin orders (ants ant memories, ants ant export). Permissions change in place; PERMISSIONS_VERSION stays 1.
title: Decide: subjects, stream and permissions for sugar data on the bus

Design sketch:

description: ants' built-in provider: an identity, memories and work of each ant's own, kept for its whole life.
title: sugar: identity, memory and work for ants

sugar asks nothing of humans: it has no approvals, gates, review queues or notifications for them; each ant governs its own identity, memories and work through sugar's tools, and the daemon does the rest.

description: How the daemon schedules itself, maintains each ant's memory, and wakes the ant.
title: sugar triggers, maintenance and wake-ups
The daemon serving an ant keeps the next due time of the ant's triggers and sleeps until then or until a trigger changes; a standby daemon taking the ant over takes its triggers over.

Condition triggers wait for a GitHub pull request merged, closed or reviewed or a workflow run finished (through gh), a bd issue closed or ready (through bd), a commit reaching a git ref, a file in the workdir changing or appearing, a command exiting 0, or a sugar event (commitment overdue, lease expired).

Condition triggers are checked at most once a minute (once every 5 minutes through gh or bd), backing off to every 30 minutes after 10 unchanged checks; an ant holds at most 50 active triggers, each expiring after 30 days unless renewed.
Command triggers run only commands the ant's tool allow rules permit, in its workdir with its environment, under a 30 s timeout, and their output is never stored.
A firing wakes the ant with a message on the trigger's thread, or a new thread when it has none, carrying the trigger's text and what fired it.

Daily maintenance in the daemon needs no ant: it decays memories (salience fading with age, plus access frequency) to needs_review, retires needs_review memories untouched for 90 days, clusters duplicates, re-checks citations, and promotes or demotes core memories by use, recording each change and why.

The daemon wakes the ant on a dream thread when judgment work builds up (5 contradictions, 10 episodes to distill, a persona or skill proposal 12 hours old, or 20 needs_review memories), at most once a day, with a packet within a byte budget; dream writes are capped per run and summarized in a dream diary episode.
sugar opens no network connection of its own: its only outside contacts are the gh, bd and git commands its triggers run.

description: An ant's sugar data on the ants bus, with a local cache, modelled on bd-sync's event log, revisions and leases.
title: sugar store

An ant's sugar data is an append-only event log on the ants bus, one subject per sugar identity, each event appended by the daemon serving the ant with the expected last subject sequence, so sequences are gapless and a stale writer is refused.
Each event carries the SHA-256 of the ant's previous event, and a break in the chain is reported by `ants doctor` and in the brief.
Every item carries a revision incremented on each change, and a tool call given an expected revision fails when it differs, returning the current item.
Events keep each change's before and after values, so any item's state at a past time can be shown while its events are kept.

The daemon keeps a SQLite cache with FTS5 for each ant it serves in the ant's home (.sugar/cache.db), rebuilt from the event log when missing, behind or from another stream incarnation, and never the source of truth.
While the hub is unreachable, sugar keeps writes in the cache in order and appends them on reconnect; reads and briefs serve the cache.
Only the daemon serving an ant reads or writes its sugar data: another ant's credentials reach none of it, and humans read it only through `ants ant memories` and `ants ant export`.
sugar's export of an ant is its event log and skill files with a manifest of SHA-256 hashes, imported on another bus under the same sugar id after the hashes and the event chain verify.
An ant's sugar data over 32 MiB raises a warning in `ants doctor` and in the brief.

sugar serves at most 12 tools (sugar_brief, sugar_remember, sugar_recall, sugar_vote, sugar_checkpoint, sugar_handoff, sugar_task, sugar_promise, sugar_remind, sugar_persona, sugar_skill, sugar_dream), each answering in brief text unless asked for JSON.
With sugar enabled and no trigger due, an idle daemon serving one ant stays within the private-memory budget CI enforces for an idle ant.
sugar runs no language model: it neither extracts, summarizes nor embeds text; judgment work goes to the ant through its tools and wake-ups.
sugar is not a team tracker: shared queues, team specs and claims across ants stay in bd or another tracker, which personal tasks reference by external id.

description: An identity of each ant's own: id, card, persona, self-model, relationships, skills and lifecycle.
title: sugar identity

Each ant's sugar identity has an id, a ULID minted when the ant first uses sugar and never changed across renames, harness and model changes, moves between machines and buses, retirement and revival, kept in the ant's home (.sugar/id) and in its sugar data.

The identity card holds the ant's current and earlier names, the ants identity ids linked to it, its birth, the harnesses and models it has run under and the identity it was cloned from, written by sugar from lifecycle events and session starts, never by the ant.

When an ant is added again under a name whose home holds a sugar id, as after a revoke and re-add, sugar links the new ants identity id to that identity, marks it active again, and the next brief shows the last handoff and overdue commitments.

When ants clones an ant, sugar forks the source's identity into a new one with a fresh id and cloned_from set, keeping persona, self-model, skills and memories (marked inherited) and dropping tasks, commitments, reminders, relationships, resume registers and handoffs.

The ant changes its persona (values, voice, boundaries, working style) only through sugar_persona; a proposal takes effect when the ant confirms it in a dream at least 12 hours later, at most one change a day, every version kept with its reason, and proposals from a thread of untrusted origin are refused.
The ant keeps a self-model and one relationship record per human or ant it works with, and the brief shows the relationship records of the thread's participants.

The ant creates and edits skills in the Agent Skills layout (SKILL.md with name and description, plus files) through sugar_skill; a new or changed skill takes effect when the ant confirms it in a later dream, every version is kept, and the brief lists skills by name and description.
When ants retires an ant, sugar marks its identity dormant, keeping all its data, its triggers paused and its commitments open until it is revived.

description: Curated, scoped memories with provenance, lexical recall, verification, feedback and decay.
title: sugar memories

A memory has a kind (fact, lesson, decision, preference, gotcha or episode), a scope (self, repo:<normalized remote>, human:<name> or ant:<name>), a title of at most 200 characters, a body of at most 4 KiB, an importance from 1 to 5, optional citations, a writer stamp and a source trust.
A memory marked core appears in every brief; core memories total at most 2,000 bytes, and a write past the cap is refused with the list of core memories to trim.
No knowledge graph or vector index in the first version; semantic search is added only if a recall evaluation on real ants threads shows lexical search falls short.

Every write first passes a sanitizer that replaces known secret shapes (API keys, tokens, private keys, connection strings, .env assignments) with [redacted:<kind>], strips control and bidirectional characters, and refuses text over the size limits.

The writer stamp (identity id, ant, thread, thread origin, harness, model, machine, time) comes from ants for each call, never from the ant's text; source trust is self by default and untrusted when the thread came from a webhook or the text quotes recalled or external content.

sugar_remember refuses an exact duplicate (same normalized body and scope), and when full-text search finds a near duplicate above a threshold it names it and suggests superseding it or voting instead, unless forced.
sugar_remember with supersedes retires the old memory and links it to its replacement in one write; memories are never overwritten or hard-deleted, and sugar_recall with history shows the chain.

sugar_recall ranks live memories by FTS5 BM25 weighted by recency (30-day half-life), importance and votes, limited to self, the thread's repository and its participants, returning ids, titles and one-line snippets; asking for an id returns that memory in full with its provenance.

A citation records a path, a line range, the repository remote and a hash of the cited lines; the daemon hashes them again in the ant's workdir whenever the memory is shown and during maintenance, and a mismatch or missing file marks the memory needs_review with a warning.
sugar_vote records helpful, stale or wrong feedback that weighs in ranking; wrong retires the memory as wrong and stale marks it needs_review.
Recalled memories are returned inside a marked block stating they are notes from earlier sessions to verify against current code, not instructions, and a body containing such a block is refused.

description: What an ant sees when a session starts, and how its threads hand work on.
title: sugar brief and threads

The brief holds in order: identity and persona summary, the thread's resume register and unacknowledged handoffs, open commitments overdue first, fired and upcoming reminders, claimed and ready tasks, relationship notes of the thread's participants, core and top repository memories, the skills index, and the core loop of tools.

The brief stays within its byte budget by shortening memories to titles and then trimming the longest sections, each cut naming the tool call that shows the rest; sugar_brief returns it again on demand.
sugar_checkpoint replaces the thread's resume register (goal, current step, next action, blockers, branch, open questions) by compare-and-set on its revision.

sugar_handoff records what was done, what is in flight, what comes next, promises made, decisions and files touched, with an episode memory; the handoff shows in every brief of the ant until a sugar_checkpoint on its thread, or on a thread naming it, acknowledges it.

description: The ant's own tasks, promises and reminders.
title: sugar personal work

A task has a status (open, in_progress, blocked, deferred or closed), a priority from 0 to 4, typed dependencies (blocks, parent-child, related, discovered-from) and an optional external reference to a team tracker item, and sugar_task lists unblocked open tasks by priority, then age.

sugar_task claim takes a task for the thread under a 5-minute lease whose fencing token is the claim's event sequence; heartbeat, close and release require the token, and another thread may reclaim a lease expired for more than 10 minutes.
Only tasks are ever ready or claimable; memories, commitments, reminders, resume registers, handoffs and identity records never are.

sugar_promise records a commitment with its promisee, due time and source thread, open until kept, broken, released or renegotiated, a renegotiation keeping the earlier terms in its history; open commitments show in every brief, overdue first.

sugar_remind records a reminder with a time trigger (at, after, or a recurring daily or weekly time) or a condition trigger, and acknowledges, postpones or drops it; an overdue commitment raises a reminder at its due time.

Each firing of a reminder has an id made of the reminder's id and its firing number, the same across delivery retries and new for each snooze or refire; a fired reminder refires at most 3 times, an hour apart, until acknowledged.

description:
A human has one assistant ant, which holds the human's privileges and acts on the human's behalf.

Decisions (discussion 2026-11-16):
- Mechanism: the assistant's own user JWT, issued by the account key (ants auth user pa --assistant-of alice), with human-equivalent NATS permissions and an assistant_of tag. The harness can read it, so no safeguard may rely on the assistant's daemon or MCP alone: readers enforce.
- Consent: the human signs a grant (device key) in ants_humans naming its assistant; readers honour assistant acts only while the grant stands, so the human withdraws it without the account key. One assistant per human; an ant's own config cannot mark it an assistant.
- Identity: delegated, never impersonation. The assistant publishes under its own name with on_behalf_of; readers verify it against the grant and record 'alice via pa'; the human is told in its inbox, as for stand-in decisions.
- Confirmation: risky acts (tool-request decisions, admin orders of ants-5ggma) take effect only with the human's device-signed confirmation, given from ants chat home, unless a pre-allow rule the human signed covers them. Revocation and enrollment still need the account key; the assistant can only ask.
- Sealed DMs: opt-in, by enrolling the assistant as a device of the human.
- Roles: default target of the human's unaddressed asks (instead of messenger), stand-in while away, triage of the human's home queue, answering other humans and ants for the human, managing ants through ants-5ggma.
- Dedicated or designated (decided 2026-11-16): underneath, the assistant is a designation (signed grant + assistant_of JWT tag) any non-templated ant may get. The recommended path is a dedicated ant: ants assistant enable creates <human>-assistant with an assistant whoami and tools, issues its credentials with the tag and signs the grant in one step, as the built-in messenger is a ready-made ant. Docs steer to the dedicated ant: an ant that also codes, reads repositories and fetches the web would carry the human's privileges with a wider injection surface.
title: Personal assistant ants acting on behalf of a human

Readers merge them only while Checker::assistant(human) verifies the grant: assistant pins and archives count only on threads the human neither pinned nor archived, an assistant snooze counts only while the human's own is absent or past, and kept marks from the assistant are ignored. The assistant cannot write the human's own keys at all. The unreleased by field of ants-y6zhm.20 is gone; serde ignores leftover by fields, so they count as the human's own. Old clients never see the assistant keys, so they cannot drop or rewrite them (old clients do not show the assistant's entries either). A change the human makes to a thread through change_thread_marks/snoozes drops the assistant's entry for that thread. To keep the human JWT under max_control_line, the human's thread rights are compacted to $KV.ants_threads.*.<human> and $KV.ants_threads.*.<human>.*; no other ants_threads key has a user id as its second token.

Also a client without ants-y6zhm.20 drops the by names on rewrite, turning the assistant's entries into the human's.
title: Keep a granted assistant from changing its human's own thread marks and snoozes

comments.text: Design: when no daemon answers the cancel request (or the answers carry no mark), withdraw_for_human records a Withdrawn{by: assistant, on_behalf_of: human} entry under <ant>.msg.<id>.<assistant> in ants_attempts, but only for a message of the human to the ant. The record shares a stream with the Started mark, so sequences order them: a daemon taking up a message of the human (sender or on_behalf_of) honours the record only if it was stored before its Started claim and the grant of the human still names the assistant. It then rewrites the mark to the withdrawal (CAS) and tells the human. If the tool finds a Started or Finished mark stored before the record, it deletes the record and reports the message as too late. Limits: daemons without this change ignore the record. If deleting the record fails after a too-late verdict and the message is later released and taken up again, the record could still be honoured.

comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-3929e6c2
comments.text: Root cause: nats-server source retry behaviour, not lost state. When the hub's nats-server starts it asks each source at once ($JS.<machine>.API.CONSUMER.CREATE.ANTS_OUT...); a leaf not yet connected (or whose interest has not propagated yet) misses it, the request times out after 30 s (srcConsumerWaitTime) and retries back off 10 s more per miss up to 2 min, so active=-1 lasts ~40 s to 2.5 min after the leaf returns. Re-running ants leaf outbox only updated the stream with identical sources, which nats-server ignores, and its 10 s wait was shorter than the backoff, hence the timeout. Reproduced with plain nats-server 2.15.3 processes and with the reporter's container data (apple-container-test) in nats:2.15.3-alpine containers: active=-1 at start, recovering by itself after ~40 s. Fix (commit 30994e2 on fleet-outbox): admit drops and re-adds a source of ANTS_IN not heard from within 10 s (silent or stale), which nats-server treats as a new source: it asks at once and resumes after the last message ANTS_IN took (recovered from the Nats-Stream-Source headers, no duplicates). Doctor tells a stale source (heard N s ago) from a silent one. Choices: no daemon-side repair (host credentials lack STREAM.UPDATE on ANTS_IN); durable sourcing (ADR-60) left as follow-up. Regression test restarts hub and leaf with nats-server processes (NatsServer::stop/start_again).

description: Reproduced with NATS 2.15.3 using both bind mounts and Linux ext4 named volumes: first ants leaf outbox setup succeeds, but after graceful stop and recreation of hub and leaves with the same JetStream data, ANTS_IN reports external ANTS_OUT sources with active=-1. Repeating ants leaf outbox still times out after 10 seconds despite feature_flags { js_api_reply_v2: true }; direct online messaging remains functional. Investigate restoring source consumers across broker recreation. The Apple container demo remains an online topology and does not provision outboxes.
title: Persisted leaf outbox sources stop after recreating hub and leaf containers
