acceptance_criteria:
- `ants update --check` and `ants update` work on macOS, Linux and Windows against a real release.
- A checksum mismatch, a missing asset or an unsupported target leaves the binary untouched with a clear error.
- The replacement is atomic: an interrupted update never leaves a partial executable.
- docs/cli.md, README.md (Install a release) and docs/operations.md document the command.
close_reason: ants update [--check] [--version V] [--pre]: SHA256SUMS-verified, atomic replace, Windows rename-aside; tested against v0.1.0 on macOS
description: Add `ants update` to install a published release in place of the running binary. Today an upgrade means downloading an archive by hand (README, Install a release) or running cargo install; the services already restart onto a replaced executable (--upgrade-check, exit 75, docs/operations.md).
design:
- Resolve the target release from the GitHub API: the latest by default, `--version vX.Y.Z` for a specific one, pre-releases only with `--pre`. `--check` only reports whether a newer release exists (exit status distinguishes up to date from update available).
- Pick the archive for the compiled target (x86_64/aarch64 linux-gnu, aarch64-apple-darwin, x86_64-pc-windows-msvc); refuse on other targets.
- Download over the existing hyper + rustls client, honour HTTPS_PROXY. Verify the archive against the release's SHA256SUMS (decision: SHA256SUMS only, no signing key for now).
- Extract the binary (tar.gz; zip on Windows), run it with --version as a smoke test, write it beside std::env::current_exe() and rename over it atomically. On Windows rename the running exe aside first (ants.exe.old, removed on the next run).
- Refuse, printing the right command, when the executable is not writable or lives under ~/.cargo/bin (cargo install users run cargo install).
- Running services pick the new binary up through --upgrade-check; print that, and the restart commands when an upgrade check is disabled.
- Keep the footprint small: weigh flate2/tar/zip against shelling out to tar; no new TLS stack; licenses through deny.toml.
title: ants update: replace the ants binary with a GitHub release

comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-003b2bf9
comments.text:
ants-9lar (branch fleet-windows, commits afd9acb 79131ff 4a0a810) makes the workspace build for Windows: clippy -D warnings clean for x86_64-pc-windows-gnu and -msvc, ants.exe linked with llvm-mingw from macOS; CI gains a windows-latest job (clippy, the MCP named pipe test, release build). Not run on Windows here: no Windows machine or Wine (arm64 Mac without Rosetta). Still to verify on a real Windows 10/11 machine:

BUILD: install Rust 1.100+ and Visual Studio Build Tools (C++ workload), then in a checkout: `cargo build --release` (target\release\ants.exe), or `cargo install --locked --path crates/ants`. Alternative: cross-build from macOS/Linux with `rustup target add x86_64-pc-windows-gnu` and mingw-w64 on PATH: `cargo build --release --target x86_64-pc-windows-gnu`. Also run `cargo test -p ants-daemon --lib -- mcp::tests::the_socket_serves_the_tools_after_the_token keystore` there.

1. Key store round trip (interactive desktop logon with password, nats-server running, human creds issued with `ants auth user NAME --human`):
   - `ants --nats URL --creds C:\path\me.creds keys store` -> "seed moved to the OS credential store, key U..."; the file now holds the JWT and the key reference only; `cmdkey /list:ants:*` (or Credential Manager > Windows Credentials) shows generic credential `ants:U...`, persistence Local computer.
   - `ants --nats URL --creds C:\path\me.creds whoami` (or `ants doctor`) connects using the stored seed; `ants doctor` reports the stored key OK.
   - `ants --nats URL --creds ... keys store` again -> "already in the OS credential store".
   - `ants --creds ... keys unstore` -> seed back in the file, credential `ants:U...` gone (`cmdkey /list:ants:*`).
   - store again, then `ants --creds ... keys remove` -> file and credential both gone.
2. A connection with a .creds naming a stored key: `ants add dev-a --store-key ...` (or keys store on an ant's creds), then `ants daemon --config ...` serving dev-a connects and answers `ants ask dev-a "hi" --wait`; delete the credential with `cmdkey /delete:ants:U...` and restart: the daemon must stop dev-a at once naming the missing entry.
3. SSH key-auth session: enable OpenSSH Server, log in with a public key (no password), run `ants --creds <stored file> whoami` -> must fail with "Windows Credential Manager: ... (os error 1312): this logon session has no credential set, as with an SSH session authenticated by key, ... keep the seed in the file (`ants keys unstore`)". Logging in over SSH with the password should instead succeed.
4. Service as another account: `schtasks /Create /SC ONSTART /RU OTHERUSER /RP * /TN ants-test /TR "C:\...\ants.exe --creds C:\...\stored.creds daemon --config ..."` (another account, or SYSTEM via /RU SYSTEM): it must not read the first user's credential (no entry / error 1312 named); then as the same user with "Run whether user is logged on or not" and the password stored it should work, and with "Do not store password" it fails with 1312.
5. Windows-specific bits of ants-9lar worth checking in the same session: a harness without HTTP MCP (e.g. one configured in [harnesses.X] lacking HTTP MCP) gets tools through `ants mcp --socket \\.\pipe\ants-mcp-<hex>`; another local user cannot open the pipe (e.g. from a second account: `[System.IO.Pipes.NamedPipeClientStream]::new('.', 'ants-mcp-<hex>').Connect(1000)` -> access denied); `copilot` installed by npm (copilot.cmd) starts as the harness; Ctrl-C / closing the console stops the daemon cleanly.

On a locked keyring whose unlock prompt cannot show (headless service), secret-tool may exit non-zero with no output, or zero with empty output, which would read as a missing entry (a hard error at daemon start and in ants doctor) rather than keystore::Unavailable (waited for). Verify on GNOME Keyring and KWallet without a session and classify the result, e.g. by checking the collection's Locked property over D-Bus or secret-tool's stderr.
title: Tell a locked Secret Service keyring from a missing entry in secret-tool lookup

close_reason: MCP test homes are now unique per process and call (target/mcp-t/<name>-<pid>-<n>) behind a Home guard removed on drop; restart tests reuse their own home. Commit 33f73555 on f2-tests.

comments.author: Quang Le/copilot-7ddb8d1d
comments.text: No spec: Test-process isolation; no user-visible behavior requirement.

description: crates/ants-daemon/src/mcp/tests/mod.rs:47-51 uses target/mcp-t/<name>, recursively removing that shared path before each test. Concurrent cargo test processes in the same checkout can delete or overwrite each other's persisted MCP state. During ants-dfxtt validation the full suite failed at replies.rs:81 (the restarted MCP no longer claimed the stored ask); the isolated test passed immediately. Give each test process or case an isolated short temporary home while preserving intentional within-test restarts.
title: MCP test homes collide between concurrent test processes
